It is set apart and cannot be used for any other purpose. To do so would be disrespect. "Devoted things, both of man and beast, are most holy to the Lord. “They cannot sell or redeem them. Once the Israelites gave the devoted thing to the Lord, they reckoned it as belonging to the Lord." No one dared to reclaim it. The giver might have made his offering with reluctance and a lack of enthusiasm. But, once made, the matter was out of his hands. By God's own law, the gift became "most holy unto the Lord."” It was not the intention of the giver that made it holy, but the holiness of the receiver. “The altar sanctifies the gift.” And an offering once laid upon the altar, from that moment belonged to the L ord. I can imagine the one who had deposited a gift. He might then doubt his sincerity and honesty in doing so. He would return to the priest, anxious about his sincerity. I am sure the priest would have silenced him at once. He would have said, "I do not know your motives in giving your offering." The facts are that you did give it, and that it is the Lord’s, for every devoted thing is most holy unto Him. "It is too late to recall the transaction now." All Israel, not just the priest, would be shocked at a man who, having offered his gift, tried to take it back. And yet, day after day, earnest Christians, who would shudder at a Jew's disrespect, are guilty of a similar act. They consecrate themselves to the Lord, then take it back through unbelief. Because God is not visibly present to the eye, it is difficult to feel that a transaction with Him is real. If, when we consecrated ourselves, we could see Him, it would feel real. We would know we had given our word and could not take it back, no matter how much we might want to. It would have to us the binding power of a spoken promise to an earthly friend. It always has that power to a man of honor. We need to see that God's presence is always a certain fact. Every act of our soul is done right before Him. A word spoken in prayer is as really spoken to Him, as if our eyes could see Him and our hands could touch Him. Then, we will no longer have vague ideas about our relations with Him. We will feel the weight of every word we say in His presence. I know some will say, "Ah, yes. “But, if He would only speak to me and say that He took me when I gave myself to Him, I would then believe it." "No, of course you would not. But, He does not usually say this until the soul has first proved its loyalty by believing what He has already said. It is he that believes who has the witness, not he that doubted. And by His very command to us to present ourselves to Him as a living sacrifice, He has pledged Himself to receive us. I cannot imagine an honorable man asking another to give him a thing he was doubtful about taking. I can imagine even less a loving parent acting so towards a darling child. “My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways .” Proverbs 23:26.This is a sure warrant. It means that th e moment the heart is given, it will be taken by the One who has commanded the gift. We must, then, feel the utmost confidence. When we surrender to the Lord, as He commands, He then receives us. From that moment, we are His. A real transaction has taken place. It cannot be violated without dishonor on our part. We know He will not violate it. In Deut. 26:17- 19 shows God's way of working: “You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, and keep his statutes and his commandments and his rules, and will obey his voice. And the LORD has declared today that you are a people for his treasured possession, as he has promised you, and that you are to keep all his commandments, and that he will set you in praise and in fame and in honor high above all nations that he has made, and that you shall be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised .” We declare the Lord our God. We will walk in His ways and keep His commandments. He declares us to be His, and we must keep all His commandments. And from that moment, He takes possession of us. This has always been His principle of working, and it continues to be so. “Every devoted thing is most holy to the Lord.” This is so plain that it admits no question. But, if you stil l doubt, let me refer you to a New Testament declaration. It approaches the subject differently, but it settles it, I think, quite definitively. It is in 1 John 5:14- 15, and reads: “ And this is the confidence that we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked of him .” Is it according to His will that you should be fully consecrated to Him? There can be, of course, but one answer to this, for He has commanded it. Is it not also according to His will that He should work in you to will and to do of His good pleasure? This question also can have but one answer, for He has declared it to be His purpose. You know, then, that these things are according to His will. So, on God's word, you must know that He hears you. Now, you must go further. You must know that you have the petitions you desired of Him. That you have, I say, not will have, or may have, but have now in actual possession. It is so that we “ Obtain promises” by faith. It is so that we have “access by faith” into the grace that is given us in our Lord Jesus Christ. Only by this do we know our hearts are "purified by faith." We can then live, stand, and walk by faith. I want to make this subject so clear and practical that no one will have further trouble with it. So, I will repeat what your soul must do to resolve your doubts about consecration. I trust you have faith in the Lord Jesus to forgive your sins. I hope you know what it is to belong to God's family and to be an heir of God through faith in Christ. And now you feel springing up in your soul the longing to be conformed to the image of your Lord. You must fully surrender yourself to Him. Only then may He work in you all the good pleasure of His will. You have tried to do this, but with no success. I want to help you now. Now, you must come to Him again. Surrender your whole self to His will, as completely as you can. You must ask Him to show you any hidden rebellion by His Spirit. If he reveals nothing, believe there is none. Your surrender is complete. We must, then, consider this a settled matter. You have abandoned yourself to the Lord. From now on, you do not belong to yourself. Never listen to any suggestion to the contrary. If you wonder if you've fully surrendered, assert that you have. Do not even argue the matter. Repel any such idea without hesitation and with firm resolve. You meant it then, you mean it now, you have accomplished it. Your emotions may clamor against the surrender, but your will must hold firm. God looks at your purpose, not your feelings about it. So, your will is all you need to attend to. Having made a surrender, never question or recall it. Next, believe that God takes what you have surrendered. Reckon it is His. Not that it will be at some future time, but is now; and that He has begun to work in you to will, and to do, of His good pleasure. And here you must rest. You have nothing more to do. You belong to the Lord now, completely in His hands. He has taken on the care and management of you. He will, as His word says, "work in you that which is well-pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ." But you must maintain a firm grip here. If you doubt your surrender, or God's acceptance of it, your faith will waver. A wavering faith will lead to a shaky experience, and He cannot work. But, while you trust He works, His work changes you. It makes you more like Christ, from glory to glory, by His mighty Spirit. Do you, now, at this moment, surrender yourself wholly to Him? You answer, yes. Then, my dear friend, reckon that you are His. He has taken you. He is working in you to will and to do of His good pleasure. And keep on reckoning this. It will help you to put your thoughts into words. Say to yourself and to God, "Lord, I am yours. I yield myself to you, and I believe you do take me." I leave myself with you. "Work in me all the good pleasure of thy will. I will only lie still in thy hands and trust you." Make this a daily act of your will. Many times a day, return to it as your constant attitude before Him. Confess it to yourself. Confess it to your God. Confess it to your friends. Always declare the Lord as your God. Commit to walking in His ways and keeping His laws. You will then find that He has claimed you as His special people. You must keep all His commandments and be "a holy people unto the Lord, as He has spoken." You may find a few simple rules helpful here. I advise using them in daily devotions. They should test the soul until we gain clarity on this matter. I. State clearly your faith in Christ as your Saviour. Also, acknowledge that you believe He has reconciled you to God, as per 2 Cor. 5:18- 19 “ All this is from God, who through Christ reconciled us to himself and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.” II. Definitely, acknowledge God as your Father. You are His redeemed and forgiven child, according to Galatians 4:5, “ to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.” III. Surrender completely to the Lord, body, soul, and spirit. Obey Him in everything where His will is known, per Romans. 12:12. “Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer.” IV. Believe, against all odds, that God takes what you abandon to Him. He will work in you, unless you frustrate His grace. See 2 Corinthians. 6:17- 18 “ Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty .” , and Philippians. 2:13. “For it is G od who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure.” V. Don't use your feelings to test your relations with God. Focus on your will and faith instead. And count all these steps you are now taking as settled, though the enemy may make it seem otherwise. Heb. 10:22-23. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful.” VI. Never, under any circumstances, should you doubt or feel discouraged. Remember, that all discouragement is from the devil, and refuse to admit it; according to John 14:1 “Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me ” V27 “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.” VII. Cultivate the habit of expressing your faith in clear words. Repeat often, "I am all the Lord's. He is working in me now to will and to do of His good pleasure," according to Heb. 13:21 “ equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

fields.title: Difficulties Concerning Faith
fields.body_html:
Faith is the next step after consecration, leading the soul into the fullness of Christian life. It is not a tangible feeling but simply believing God’s promises, much like trusting others in daily life. True faith means resting in God’s word without worry or doubt, trusting Him as we trust those around us. Just as slaves had to believe in their freedom to experience it, we must believe in God’s promises to receive His blessings.

Trusting God glorifies Him and leads to the fulfillment of His will in our lives .

After consecration, the next step is faith. It leads the soul out of the wilderness of Christian experience into a land flowing with milk and honey. And here, as in the first step, the enemy is very skilled at creating difficulties and obstacles. The child of God, seeing the fullness in Jesus for him, longs to grasp it. But, every teacher he asks asserts that only faith can receive it. But, his mind is a mystery about faith. This assertion, instead of helping, makes it more difficult and complex than ever.

“Of course it is to be by faith,” he says, “for I know that everything in the Christian life is by faith. But then, that is what makes it so hard, for I have no faith, and I do not even know what it is, nor how to get it.” And, baffled by this difficulty, he is plunged into despair. This trouble arises from a misunderstanding of faith. In truth, faith is the simplest thing in the world, and the easiest to attain.

Your idea of faith, I suppose, has been something like this. You view it as a sort of thing. It's either a religious exercise of the soul or a gracious disposition of the heart. It's something tangible. When you have it, you can rejoice in it. You can use it as a passport to God's favor, or a coin to buy His gifts. You have been praying for faith. You expected to get something like this. But, you never received anything.

So, you insist that you have no faith. Now faith, in fact, is not in the least this sort of thing.

It is nothing at all tangible.

It is simply believing God, and, like sight, it is nothing apart from its object. You might as well shut your eyes and look inside to see if you have sight, as to look inside to see if you have faith. You see something, and thus know that you have sight; you believe something, and thus know that you have faith. For, as sight is only seeing, so faith is only believing. The only necessary thing about seeing is, to see the thing as it is. So, the only necessary thing about believing is, to believe the thing as it is.

The virtue does not lie in your believing, but in the thing you believe. If you believe the truth, you are saved; if you believe a lie, you are lost. The belief is the same in both cases. The things believed in are exactly opposite. This is what makes the mighty difference. Your salvation comes, not because your faith saves you. It is because it links you to the Saviour who saves. Your faith is really nothing but the link.

I beg you to see, then, the simplicity of faith. It is just believing God when He says He has done something for us, or will do it. Then, we must trust Him to do it. It is so simple that it is hard to explain.

If anyone asks what it means to trust someone to do a job for me, I can only answer this: It means letting them do it. I feel it is unnecessary to do it myself. We have all trusted others with important work. We felt perfect rest in this trust. It was because we had confidence in those who took it on. How often do mothers trust their precious infants to nurses, without a hint of anxiety?

We all trust our health and lives to cooks, coachmen, engine drivers, and train conductors. We do this without fear. These paid servants could ruin us in an instant if they chose to or if they were careless.

All this we do, and make no fuss about it. We often trust people after a brief acquaintance. We need only a general knowledge of human nature and common social rules. We never feel we're doing anything remarkable. You have done all this yourself, dear reader, and are doing it continually. You could not live in this world for a day if you could not trust your fellow men. And it never enters into your head to say you cannot.

But yet you do not hesitate to say, continually, that you cannot trust your God! Please, imagine acting in your human relations as you do in your spiritual ones. Imagine you must start tomorrow with a thought in your head: you could trust nobody, as you had no faith. At breakfast, you would say, "I cannot eat anything on this table. I have no faith. I can't believe the cook hasn't poisoned the coffee. Or that the butcher hasn't sent diseased meat. So you would starve. Then, you'd say, "I cannot ride the train. “I have no faith, so I cannot trust anyone."

You would have to walk everywhere. You would grow very weary. Also, you could not reach many places you could have reached by train. When your friends or business agent brought you statements, you'd say, "I'm sorry, but I can't believe you. “I have no f aith and can't trust anyone." If you read a newspaper, you'd have to put it down. You'd say, "I can't believe a word it says. I have no faith. I don't believe there is a queen, for I've never seen her. And I don't believe in Ireland, for I've never been there." And I have no faith, so of course I cannot believe anything that I have not actually felt and touched myself. It is a great trial, but I cannot help it, for I have no faith.”

Imagine such a day. It would be disastrous for you. It would seem foolish to anyone who watched you throughout the day. Know your friends would feel insulted. Your servants would quit. Then ask yourself this: If it's so dreadful to distrust your fellow men, what of telling God you can't trust Him?

You say it's a great trial, but you can't help it; you have no faith. Can you trust your fellow men but not your God? That you can receive the “witness of men,” and cannot receive the “witness of God?” That you can believe man’s records, and cannot believe God’s record? You trust your weak, failing fellow- creatures with your dearest interests. Yet, you fear to commit your soul to the blessed Saviour.

He shed His blood to save you. He is "able to save you to the Uttermost."

Surely, dear believer, your name implies you can believe. So, you will never again dare to excuse your lack of faith. This means, of course, that you have no faith in God. You are not asked to have faith in yourself. If you did, it would be a very wrong state of soul. I beg you, when you think or say these things, to complete the sentence. Say, "I have no faith in God, I cannot believe in God." I am sure this will soon become so dreadful to you that you won't dare to continue it.

But you say, I cannot believe without the Holy Spirit. Very well; will you conclude that your want of faith is because of the failure of the blessed Spirit to do His work? If it is, then you are not to blame.

You need to feel no condemnation. All my urges to believe are useless. But, no! Do you not see that, in taking this position, you have no faith and cannot believe? You are "making God a liar." You are also showing a complete lack of trust in the Holy Spirit. For He is always ready to help our infirmities.

We never have to wait for Him, He is always waiting for us. I have complete faith in the Holy Ghost.

He is always ready to do His work. So, I say to you all: you can believe now, at this moment. If you do not, it is not the Spirit's fault, but your own.

Put your will then over on to the believing side. Say, “Lord I will believe, I do believe,” and continue to say it. Insist on believing, even when every suggestion of doubt tempts you. In your unbelief, throw yourself on God's word and promises. Dare to trust in the saving power of the Lord Jesus. If you have ever trusted a friend with something precious, I urge you to trust yourself now. Trust your spiritual interests to your Heavenly Friend. Never, never, NEVER doubt again.

And remember, trust and worry are more incompatible than oil and water. Would you call it trust? If you ask a friend to do something for you, then you spend your days and nights worrying if they will do it right. Can you call it trust? You have put your soul in the Lord's hands. But, you spend hours each day and night, filled with anxiety as you question it. When a believer really trusts anything, he ceases to worry about that thing which he has trusted.

And when he worries, it is a plain proof that he does not trust. Tested by this rule how little real trust there is in the Church of Christ! No wonder our L ord asked the pathetic question, “When the Son of Man comes shall he find faith on the earth?” He will find much activity and earnestness. There will be many devoted hearts. But, will he find faith? It is the one thing He values most. It is a solemn question, and I would that every Christian heart would ponder it well. But, may our past lives suffice us. We have shared in the world's unbelief. So, let us, who know our blessed Lord, prove His truth.

His trustworthiness is beyond words. We must, with our hearts, trust Him fully.

I remember, very early in my Christian life, an appeal in a volume of old sermons. It stirred my every tender and loyal impulse. It urged all who loved the Lord Jesus to show others His worthiness by their own steadfast faith in Him. I remember my soul cried out with a longing. I longed to walk those dark paths. My total distrust would be a blessed, glorious privilege.

"You have not passed this way before," it may be. But today, it is your happy privilege to prove, as never before, your loyal confidence in the Lord. Start with Him on a life of faith, lived in absolute, childlike trust in Him. You have trusted Him in a few things, and He has not failed you. Trust Him now for everything. See if He does not do for you more than you could ever ask or think. It won't be by your strength, but by His mighty power. It will work in you all the good pleasure of His most blessed will.

You trust the Lord to manage the universe and all creation. Can your case be more complex than these?

You need not be anxious about his management of it. Away with such unworthy doubting! Trust in your God. Observe how all problems will vanish swiftly before a strong will to believe. Trust in the dark, the light, at night, and in the morning. You will find that, though faith may start as a mighty effort, it will become a natural habit of the soul.

All things are possible to God. Mark 11:23“And Jesus said to him , if you can’! All things are possible for one who believes" "Faith has, in the past, 'subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, waxed valiant in fight, [and] turned to fight the armies of the aliens.' And faith can do it again." Our Lord says, “Because of your little faith. For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you. “Mathew 17:20 If you are a child of God, you must have at least a mustard seed's worth of faith. So, you cannot say again that you cannot trust because you have no faith. Say, "I can trust my Lord, and I will. Not all the powers of earth or hell shall make me doubt my glorious, faithful Rede emer!"”

This century's greatest event, the emancipation of our slaves, is a great lesson in faith. The slaves received their freedom by faith, just as we must receive ours. They received the good news that the government had proclaimed their freedom. They became free the moment the Proclamation was issued.

But, they didn't truly believe it until they heard the good news. The fact had to come first. But, they had to believe before the fact was available. The feeling would follow last of all. This is the divine order always, and the order of common-sense as well.

I. The fact.

II. The faith.

III. The feeling.

But man reverses this order and says, I. The feeling. II. The faith. III. The fact. If the slaves had followed man's order about their freedom, they might have stayed in slavery for a time. They should have refused to believe it until they had felt it. I have heard of one instance where this was the case. In a remote Southern town, a Northern lady found, two or three years after the war, some slaves who hadn't claimed their freedom. An assertion of hers, that the North had set them free, aroused the attention of an old colored auntie. The auntie interrupted her with an eager question.

" Oh, miss, are we free?"

“Of course, you are," the woman replied.

“Oh, are you sure?" the woman urged, with intense eagerness.

“Certainly, I am sure,” the lady replied, her voice steady and assured. “Why, is it possible you did not know it?”

Well,” said the woman, “we heard that we were free, so we asked the master, and he said we weren’t, so we were afraid to leave. Then we heard again that we were free, so we went to the colonel, and he said we should stay with our old master. So, we’ve just been uncertain. Sometimes we thought we were free, and other times we thought we weren’t. But now, miss, if you’re sure we are free, could you tell me all about it?” Seeing that this was a real need, the lady explained everything to the poor woman.

She told her about the war, the Northern army, and Abraham Lincoln. She spoke about his Emancipation Proclamation and the freedom it brought.

The poor slave listened with the most intense eagerness. She heard the good news. She believed it. And when the story was ended, she walked out of the room with an air of the utmost independence, saying as she went, -- “I’m free! I’m not staying with that old master anymore!” She had at last received her freedom, and she had received it by faith. The government had declared her free long before. But, this had not availed her. She had never believed in this declaration. The good news had not profited her, not being “mixed with faith” in the one who heard it. But now she believed, and believing, she dared to reckon herself to be free. And this, not due to any change in herself or her surroundings, nor to any feelings of her own heart. But, because she had faith in another. He had come to her with the news of her freedom.

Need I make the application? In a hundred messages, God has declared our freedom. He urges us to see ourselves as free. Let your faith then lay hold of His proclamation, and assert it to be true. Declare to yourself, to your friends, and in the secret of your soul to God, that you are free. Refuse to listen for a moment to the lying assertions of your old master that you are still his slave. Let nothing discourage you, no inward feelings nor outward signs. Hold your beliefs despite all opposition. I promise you, based on the authority of our Lord, that you will see it done according to your faith.

Of all the worships we can bring our God, none is as sweet to Him as this, our utter, self-abandoning trust. None brings Him so much glory. In every dark hour, remember this: "Now, for a time, you are in heaviness through many temptations." It is so. "Your faith's trial is more precious than gold. Gold perishes, even if fire tests it. May you find your faith to praise, honor, and bring glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ."

You trust your weak, failing fellow- creatures with your dearest interests. Yet, you fear to commit your soul to the blessed Saviour. He shed His blood to save you. He is "able to save you to the Uttermost." Surely, dear believer, your name implies you can believe. So, you will never again dare to excuse your lack of faith. This means, of course, that you have no faith in God. You are not asked to have faith in yourself. If you did, it would be a very wrong state of soul. I beg you, when you think or say these things, to complete the sentence. Say, "I have no faith in God, I cannot believe in God." I am sure this will soon become so dreadful to you that you won't dare to continue it. But you say, I cannot believe without the Holy Spirit. Very well; will you conclude that your want of faith is because of the failure of the blessed Spirit to do His work? If it is, then you are not to blame. You need to feel no condemnation. All my urges to believe are useless. But, no! Do you not see that, in taking this position, you have no faith and cannot believe? You are "making God a liar." You are also showing a complete lack of trust in the Holy Spirit. For He is always ready to help our infirmities. We never have to wait for Him, He is always waiting for us. I have complete faith in the Holy Ghost. He is always ready to do His work. So, I say to you all: you can believe now, at this moment. If you do not, it is not the Spirit's fault, but your own. Put your will then over on to the believing side. Say, “Lord I will believe, I do believe,” and continue to say it. Insist on believing, even when every suggestion of doubt tempts you. In your unbelief, throw yourself on God's word and promises. Dare to trust in the saving power of the Lord Jesus. If you have ever trusted a friend with something precious, I urge you to trust yourself now. Trust your spiritual interests to your Heavenly Friend. Never, never, NEVER doubt again. And remember, trust and worry are more incompatible than oil and water. Would you call it trust? If you ask a friend to do something for you, then you spend your days and nights worrying if they will do it right. Can you call it trust? You have put your soul in the Lord's hands. But, you spend hours each day and night, filled with anxiety as you question it. When a believer really trusts anything, he ceases to worry about that thing which he has trusted. And when he worries, it is a plain proof that he does not trust. Tested by this rule how little real trust there is in the Church of Christ! No wonder our L ord asked the pathetic question, “When the Son of Man comes shall he find faith on the earth?” He will find much activity and earnestness. There will be many devoted hearts. But, will he find faith? It is the one thing He values most. It is a solemn question, and I would that every Christian heart would ponder it well. But, may our past lives suffice us. We have shared in the world's unbelief. So, let us, who know our blessed Lord, prove His truth. His trustworthiness is beyond words. We must, with our hearts, trust Him fully. I remember, very early in my Christian life, an appeal in a volume of old sermons. It stirred my every tender and loyal impulse. It urged all who loved the Lord Jesus to show others His worthiness by their own steadfast faith in Him. I remember my soul cried out with a longing. I longed to walk those dark paths. My total distrust would be a blessed, glorious privilege. "You have not passed this way before," it may be. But today, it is your happy privilege to prove, as never before, your loyal confidence in the Lord. Start with Him on a life of faith, lived in absolute, childlike trust in Him. You have trusted Him in a few things, and He has not failed you. Trust Him now for everything. See if He does not do for you more than you could ever ask or think. It won't be by your strength, but by His mighty power. It will work in you all the good pleasure of His most blessed will. You trust the Lord to manage the universe and all creation. Can your case be more complex than these? You need not be anxious about his management of it. Away with such unworthy doubting! Trust in your God. Observe how all problems will vanish swiftly before a strong will to believe. Trust in the dark, the light, at night, and in the morning. You will find that, though faith may start as a mighty effort, it will become a natural habit of the soul. All things are possible to God. Mark 11:23“And Jesus said to him , if you can’! All things are possible for one who believes" "Faith has, in the past, 'subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, waxed valiant in fight, [and] turned to fight the armies of the aliens.' And faith can do it again." Our Lord says, “Because of your little faith. For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you. “Mathew 17:20 If you are a child of God, you must have at least a mustard seed's worth of faith. So, you cannot say again that you cannot trust because you have no faith. Say, "I can trust my Lord, and I will. Not all the powers of earth or hell shall make me doubt my glorious, faithful Rede emer!"” This century's greatest event, the emancipation of our slaves, is a great lesson in faith. The slaves received their freedom by faith, just as we must receive ours. They received the good news that the government had proclaimed their freedom. They became free the moment the Proclamation was issued. But, they didn't truly believe it until they heard the good news. The fact had to come first. But, they had to believe before the fact was available. The feeling would follow last of all. This is the divine order always, and the order of common-sense as well. I. The fact. II. The faith. III. The feeling. But man reverses this order and says, I. The feeling. II. The faith. III. The fact. If the slaves had followed man's order about their freedom, they might have stayed in slavery for a time. They should have refused to believe it until they had felt it. I have heard of one instance where this was the case. In a remote Southern town, a Northern lady found, two or three years after the war, some slaves who hadn't claimed their freedom. An assertion of hers, that the North had set them free, aroused the attention of an old colored auntie. The auntie interrupted her with an eager question. " Oh, miss, are we free?" “Of course, you are," the woman replied. “Oh, are you sure?" the woman urged, with intense eagerness. “Certainly, I am sure,” the lady replied, her voice steady and assured. “Why, is it possible you did not know it?” Well,” said the woman, “we heard that we were free, so we asked the master, and he said we weren’t, so we were afraid to leave. Then we heard again that we were free, so we went to the colonel, and he said we should stay with our old master. So, we’ve just been uncertain. Sometimes we thought we were free, and other times we thought we weren’t. But now, miss, if you’re sure we are free, could you tell me all about it?” Seeing that this was a real need, the lady explained everything to the poor woman. She told her about the war, the Northern army, and Abraham Lincoln. She spoke about his Emancipation Proclamation and the freedom it brought. The poor slave listened with the most intense eagerness. She heard the good news. She believed it. And when the story was ended, she walked out of the room with an air of the utmost independence, saying as she went, -- “I’m free! I’m not staying with that old master anymore!” She had at last received her freedom, and she had received it by faith. The government had declared her free long before. But, this had not availed her. She had never believed in this declaration. The good news had not profited her, not being “mixed with faith” in the one who heard it. But now she believed, and believing, she dared to reckon herself to be free. And this, not due to any change in herself or her surroundings, nor to any feelings of her own heart. But, because she had faith in another. He had come to her with the news of her freedom. Need I make the application? In a hundred messages, God has declared our freedom. He urges us to see ourselves as free. Let your faith then lay hold of His proclamation, and assert it to be true. Declare to yourself, to your friends, and in the secret of your soul to God, that you are free. Refuse to listen for a moment to the lying assertions of your old master that you are still his slave. Let nothing discourage you, no inward feelings nor outward signs. Hold your beliefs despite all opposition. I promise you, based on the authority of our Lord, that you will see it done according to your faith. Of all the worships we can bring our God, none is as sweet to Him as this, our utter, self-abandoning trust. None brings Him so much glory. In every dark hour, remember this: "Now, for a time, you are in heaviness through many temptations." It is so. "Your faith's trial is more precious than gold. Gold perishes, even if fire tests it. May you find your faith to praise, honor, and bring glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ."

fields.title: Difficulties Concerning The Will
fields.body_html:
After initial peace, doubts may lead believers to question their faith and feel disconnected from their emotions. The chapter emphasizes that true faith is rooted in the will, not emotions. By surrendering their will to God, believers can overcome emotional struggles and grow spiritually. Aligning the will with God's leads to victory, regardless of fluctuating feelings, and encourages Christians to trust their decision to follow God's path despite emotional turmoil.

When a child of God, with trust, abandons himself to Christ, he may know the joy of the life hid with Christ in God. But, a new difficulty may arise. After the initial peace and rest fade, he feels an utter unreality in his experiences. If those feelings never came, he feels a hypocrite for thinking they are real. He thinks his belief is shallow, a lip-service. So, it is worthless. His surrender is not from the heart, so it cannot please God.

He fears to say he is the Lord's, for it may be untrue. Yet, he cannot deny it, as he longs for it so. The difficulty is real and disheartening. But, it will be easily overcome. The Christian must understand the new life and learn to live in it. People believe that "life hid with Christ in God" means to trust emotions.

So, the soul focuses on them. If they are satisfying, the soul rests. If not, it is troubled. Now, the truth is, this life is not to be lived in emotions. It is to be lived in the will. So, the varying emotional states do not affect life. If the will remains steadfast in its center, God's will.

To make this plain, I must enlarge a little. Fenelon says somewhere that “pure religion resides in the will alone.” He means that the will is the governing power in a man's nature. If the will is set straight, then all his nature must harmonize. By the will I do not mean the man's wish, nor his purpose. I mean the choice, the deciding power, and the king, to which all in the man must obey. It is the man, in short, the “Ego,” that which we feel to be ourselves. It is sometimes thought that emotions are the governing power in our nature. But, from experience, we know there is something within us. It is behind our emotions and wishes. It is an independent self that decides and controls everything.

Our emotions are ours. We suffer and enjoy them. But, they are not ourselves. If God is to possess us, He must enter our central will or personality. If He reigns there by the power of His Spirit, all of our nature must submit to Him. As the will is, so is the man. This truth is very relevant to the difficulty I am considering. Our will often opposes our emotions. If we trust our emotions, we may feel like hypocrites.

We would be declaring real what our will alone has decided. But if we see the will as king, we will ignore any protest. We will accept its decisions as real, no matter how the emotions may rebel.

I know this is a tough subject. But, it is vital to the life of faith. So, I urge you, dear reader, to stick with it until you master it. An example may help. A young man, eager to start a new life, was very smart.

But, he was a slave to a strong habit of doubting. This discouraged him. To his emotions, nothing seemed true or real. The more he struggled, the more unreal it all became. He was told a secret about the will. It was, if he chose to believe, to put his will on the believing side. In short, he must say, "I will believe!" I do believe!” He need not worry about his emotions. They would, eventually, find harmony.

“What!” He said, "Do you mean I can choose to believe that, when nothing seems true to me? “Will that belief be real?" "Yes. Your task is this: put your will on God's side in this matter of believing. If you do this, God will take possession of it. He will work in you to will His good pleasure. Soon, you will find that He has subdued your whole nature to Hi mself."” “Well,” was the answer, “I can do this?

I cannot control my emotions. But, I can control my will. The new life seems possible, if only my will needs to be set straight. "I can give my will to God, and I do!" From that moment, he ignored his emotions.

They accused him of being a hypocrite. This young man held on to his decision. He answered every accusation with a firm belief. He chose to believe; he meant to believe; he did believe. After a few days, he triumphed. Every emotion and thought was now captive to the mighty power of the blessed Spirit of God. He had given his will to God.

He had held fast his faith without wavering. Yet, he felt he had no real faith to hold fast. At times, it drained all his will to say he believed. It was so contrary to all his senses and feelings. But, he knew his will was, after all, himself. If he kept it on God's side, he was doing all he could. Only God could change his emotions or control his being. It has produced one of the grandest Christian lives I know. It is a life of marvelous simplicity, directness, and power over sin. The secret lies just here. Our will, the source of all our actions, is, in its natural state, under the control of self. But, self has been working it in us to our ruin and misery. Now God says, "Yield yourselves to me, as those alive from the dead. I will work in you to will and to do my good pleasure.”

The moment we yield ourselves, He takes possession of us. He works in us "that which is well pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship . “ Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect . (Rom. 12:1-2.)Let us take another illustration. A lady, hidden with Christ, faced a great trial. Every emotion within her rebelled against it. If she'd considered her feelings her king, she'd have been in despair. But she had learned this secret of the will. Knowing, at her core, she chose God's will for her, she ignored her emotions.

She met every anxious thought about the trial with the words, repeated over and over, "Your will be done!" Your will be done!” She chose to submit her will to God's. His will should be, and was, her delight. In a very short time, every thought was subdued. She even found her emotions rejoicing in God's will.

Again, there was a lady who had a besetting sin, which in her emotions she dearly loved, but which in her will she hated. She believed she must control her emotions. So, she thought she couldn't conquer them unless her emotions changed first. But she learned a secret about the will. Going to her knees, she said, "Lord, You see that, with one part of my nature, I love this sin. But, in my true self, I hate it." And now I put my will over on thy side in the matter. I will not do it anymore. Do you deliver me.”

Immediately, God took over the will she had surrendered to Him. He began to work in her. His will then mastered her emotions. She found herself delivered, not by an outward command, but by an inward power.

The Spirit of God working in her that which was well pleasing in His sight. And now, dear Christian, let me show you how to apply this principle to your difficulties. Stop considering your emotions. They are only servants. Your will is the real king in you. So, focus on it. Is that given up to God? Is that put into His hands? Does your will decide to believe? Does your will choose to obey? If this is the case, then you are in the Lord’s hands, and you decide to believe, and you choose to obey; for your will is yourself. And the thing is done. The transaction with God is as real, where only your will acts, as when every emotion coincides.

It does not seem as real to you; but in God’s sight it is as real. When you find this secret, you need not attend to your emotions. Simply focus on your will. Then, all the Scripture commands become possible to you. They include: yielding to God, being a living sacrifice, abiding in Christ, walking in the light, and dying to self. You know your will can act and take God's side in all these. But if your emotions had to do it, you would despair, knowing they are uncontrollable. So, when you feel unreal or hypocritical, do not worry. It is just your emotions and not worth a moment's thought. Only ensure your will is in God's hands. Abandon yourself to His work. Choose His side, and there leave it.

Your surging emotions, like a tossing vessel, must yield to a steady pull. This is the power of God, to which you chose to attach yourself. Your emotions must come into captivity, and give their allegiance to Him. You will prove true the say ing, “If any man will do His will, he shall know of the doctrine.”

The will is like a wise mother in a nursery; the feelings are like a set of clamoring, crying children. The mother decides upon a certain course of action, which she believes to be right and best. The children clamor against it, and declare it shall not be. But the mother, knowing she is the mistress, remains calm.

Unmoved by the children's clamors, she tries to soothe them. Eventually, the children must yield and accept her decision.

Thus order and harmony are preserved. But if that mother thought the children were the mistresses, chaos would reign. Such instances have been known in family life! And how many souls, at this very moment, are confused? They are so because feelings govern, not the will! Remember, then, that your will decides what is real. Not your emotions. It is more dangerous to be a hypocrite by trusting your feelings than to stick to your will. If your will is on God's side, you are no hypocrite. So, claim as your own the blessed reality of belonging to Him. Your emotions may say otherwise, but they don't matter.

I believe that, throughout the Bible, the "heart" does not mean emotions. It means the will, the man's true self. God's goal is to have this "I" yielded to Him, and to take full control of this central life. It is not the feelings of the man God wants, but the man himself. Have you given Him yourself, dear reader?

Have you abandoned your will to His working? Do you consent to surrender the very centre of your being into His hands? Then, let your nature's outposts clamor as they may. You can, even now, say with the apostle, "I am crucified with Christ; nevertheless, I live; yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave Himself for me."

After the chapter was sent to the printer, Pasteur T. Monod of Paris gave a remarkable, practical example of its teachings. It is a Presbyterian minister's experience. This pastor had kept it for many years.

NEWBURGH, Sept. 26, 1842.

Dear Brother, -- I take a moment of my time, devoted to the Lord, to write a short letter to you, His servant. It is sweet to feel we are wholly the Lord’s, that He has received us and called us His. Th is is religion. It is a giving up of self-ownership. It is a full embrace of the idea, "I am not my own, I am bought with a price." Since I last saw you, I have been pressing on. Yet, there is nothing remarkable in my experience to share. I do not know if it is best to seek remarkable things. But I strive to be holy, as God is holy, pressing on toward the prize.

I do not feel qualified to instruct you; I can only tell you the way in which I was led. The Lord deals differently with each soul. We should not copy others' experiences. But those seeking a clean heart must attend to certain things. We must personally consecrate all to God. We must make a covenant with Him to be wholly and forever His. I made this, using only my mind. My heart is hard and dark, full of sin and disbelief. I feel nothing. I covenanted to be the Lord’s, and laid all upon the altar, a living sacrifice, to the best of my ability. And after I rose from my knees, I was conscious of no change in my feeling.

I was painfully conscious that there was no change. But I was sure I did. With all my sincerity, I made an eternal, complete dedication of myself to God. I did not consider the work done by any means. But, I engaged to be a living, perpetual sacrifice, wholly devoted to God. And now came the effort to do this. I knew that I must believe that God did accept me, and had come in to dwell in my heart. I was conscious that I did not believe this, and yet I desired to do so. I read with much prayer John’s First Epistle, and endeavored to assure my heart of God’s love to me as an individual. I was sensible that my heart was full of evil.

I seemed to have no power to overcome pride or to repel evil thoughts, which I abhorred. But Christ was manifested to destroy the devil's works. The sin in my heart was the devil's work. I was enabled, therefore, to believe that God was working in me. He was to will and to do, while I worked out my own salvation with fear and trembling.

I was convinced of unbelief, that it was voluntary and criminal. I clearly saw that unbelief was an awful sin; it made the faithful God a liar. The Lord showed me my besetting sins. They had dominion over me. They were, especially, preaching myself instead of Christ. I also indulged in complacent thoughts after preaching. I was enabled to make myself of no reputation, and to seek the honor which cometh from God only. Satan struggled hard to beat me back from the Rock of Ages.

But thanks to God, I found a way to live in the moment. Then, I found rest.

I trusted in the blood of Jesus as a full atonement for my past sins. I committed my future to the Lord, agreeing to do His will as He revealed it. I saw that I had to look to Jesus for grace. I had to trust Him to cleanse my heart and keep me from sin now. I felt a need to depend on the grace of Christ, if only for a moment. I would not let the enemy trouble me about the past or future. I expected, each moment, a supply for that moment. I agreed to be a child of Abraham. I would walk by faith in the Word of God, not by my feelings. I would seek to be a Bible Christian. Since that time the Lord has given me a steady victory over sins which before enslaved me.

I delight in the Lord, and in His Word. I delight in my work as a minister: my fellowship is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ. I am a baby in Christ; I know my progress has been small compared with that made by many. My feelings vary. But when I feel, I praise God and trust His word.

When I'm empty and feel nothing, I do the same. I have covenanted to walk by faith and not by feelings.

The Lord is beginning to revive His work among my people. “Praise the Lord.” May the Lord fill you with all His fullness and give you all the mind of Christ. Oh, be faithful! Walk before God and be perfect. Preach the Word. Be instant in season and out of season. The Lord loves you. He works with you. Rest your soul completely upon that promise, “Look, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.”

Your fellow soldier, WILLIAM HILL There may be some who will object to this teaching, that it ignores the work of the blessed Holy Spirit.

But I must refer such to the introductory chapter of this book, in which I have fully explained myself.

I am not writing upon that side of the subject; I am considering man ’s part in the matter, and not the part of the Spirit. I know that all a man can do would be useless if the Holy Spirit did not work in him continually. I write as I do because I believe in the Spirit. It is a mighty, ever-present power, ready to do his work. But, like the wind that blows where it wants, you hear its sound. But you cannot tell where it comes from or where it goes. The Spirit's actions are beyond our control and understanding.

The results we know, and the steps on our part which lead to those results, but we know nothing more.

And yet, like a factory worker, we dare to urge men to act. They must, like the worker, trust an unseen power, called steam, behind their machinery. It can accomplish the impossible. We know the mighty Spirit will always provide the power needed for each moment's act. We boldly claim that we, as writers, can say, as earnestly as any other Christians, "We believe in the Holy Ghost."

And now, dear Christian, let me show you how to apply this principle to your difficulties. Stop considering your emotions. They are only servants. Your will is the real king in you. So, focus on it. Is that given up to God? Is that put into His hands? Does your will decide to believe? Does your will choose to obey? If this is the case, then you are in the Lord’s hands, and you decide to believe, and you choose to obey; for your will is yourself. And the thing is done. The transaction with God is as real, where only your will acts, as when every emotion coincides. It does not seem as real to you; but in God’s sight it is as real. When you find this secret, you need not attend to your emotions. Simply focus on your will. Then, all the Scripture commands become possible to you. They include: yielding to God, being a living sacrifice, abiding in Christ, walking in the light, and dying to self. You know your will can act and take God's side in all these. But if your emotions had to do it, you would despair, knowing they are uncontrollable. So, when you feel unreal or hypocritical, do not worry. It is just your emotions and not worth a moment's thought. Only ensure your will is in God's hands. Abandon yourself to His work. Choose His side, and there leave it. Your surging emotions, like a tossing vessel, must yield to a steady pull. This is the power of God, to which you chose to attach yourself. Your emotions must come into captivity, and give their allegiance to Him. You will prove true the say ing, “If any man will do His will, he shall know of the doctrine.” The will is like a wise mother in a nursery; the feelings are like a set of clamoring, crying children. The mother decides upon a certain course of action, which she believes to be right and best. The children clamor against it, and declare it shall not be. But the mother, knowing she is the mistress, remains calm. Unmoved by the children's clamors, she tries to soothe them. Eventually, the children must yield and accept her decision. Thus order and harmony are preserved. But if that mother thought the children were the mistresses, chaos would reign. Such instances have been known in family life! And how many souls, at this very moment, are confused? They are so because feelings govern, not the will! Remember, then, that your will decides what is real. Not your emotions. It is more dangerous to be a hypocrite by trusting your feelings than to stick to your will. If your will is on God's side, you are no hypocrite. So, claim as your own the blessed reality of belonging to Him. Your emotions may say otherwise, but they don't matter. I believe that, throughout the Bible, the "heart" does not mean emotions. It means the will, the man's true self. God's goal is to have this "I" yielded to Him, and to take full control of this central life. It is not the feelings of the man God wants, but the man himself. Have you given Him yourself, dear reader? Have you abandoned your will to His working? Do you consent to surrender the very centre of your being into His hands? Then, let your nature's outposts clamor as they may. You can, even now, say with the apostle, "I am crucified with Christ; nevertheless, I live; yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave Himself for me." After the chapter was sent to the printer, Pasteur T. Monod of Paris gave a remarkable, practical example of its teachings. It is a Presbyterian minister's experience. This pastor had kept it for many years. NEWBURGH, Sept. 26, 1842. Dear Brother, -- I take a moment of my time, devoted to the Lord, to write a short letter to you, His servant. It is sweet to feel we are wholly the Lord’s, that He has received us and called us His. Th is is religion. It is a giving up of self-ownership. It is a full embrace of the idea, "I am not my own, I am bought with a price." Since I last saw you, I have been pressing on. Yet, there is nothing remarkable in my experience to share. I do not know if it is best to seek remarkable things. But I strive to be holy, as God is holy, pressing on toward the prize. I do not feel qualified to instruct you; I can only tell you the way in which I was led. The Lord deals differently with each soul. We should not copy others' experiences. But those seeking a clean heart must attend to certain things. We must personally consecrate all to God. We must make a covenant with Him to be wholly and forever His. I made this, using only my mind. My heart is hard and dark, full of sin and disbelief. I feel nothing. I covenanted to be the Lord’s, and laid all upon the altar, a living sacrifice, to the best of my ability. And after I rose from my knees, I was conscious of no change in my feeling. I was painfully conscious that there was no change. But I was sure I did. With all my sincerity, I made an eternal, complete dedication of myself to God. I did not consider the work done by any means. But, I engaged to be a living, perpetual sacrifice, wholly devoted to God. And now came the effort to do this. I knew that I must believe that God did accept me, and had come in to dwell in my heart. I was conscious that I did not believe this, and yet I desired to do so. I read with much prayer John’s First Epistle, and endeavored to assure my heart of God’s love to me as an individual. I was sensible that my heart was full of evil. I seemed to have no power to overcome pride or to repel evil thoughts, which I abhorred. But Christ was manifested to destroy the devil's works. The sin in my heart was the devil's work. I was enabled, therefore, to believe that God was working in me. He was to will and to do, while I worked out my own salvation with fear and trembling. I was convinced of unbelief, that it was voluntary and criminal. I clearly saw that unbelief was an awful sin; it made the faithful God a liar. The Lord showed me my besetting sins. They had dominion over me. They were, especially, preaching myself instead of Christ. I also indulged in complacent thoughts after preaching. I was enabled to make myself of no reputation, and to seek the honor which cometh from God only. Satan struggled hard to beat me back from the Rock of Ages. But thanks to God, I found a way to live in the moment. Then, I found rest. I trusted in the blood of Jesus as a full atonement for my past sins. I committed my future to the Lord, agreeing to do His will as He revealed it. I saw that I had to look to Jesus for grace. I had to trust Him to cleanse my heart and keep me from sin now. I felt a need to depend on the grace of Christ, if only for a moment. I would not let the enemy trouble me about the past or future. I expected, each moment, a supply for that moment. I agreed to be a child of Abraham. I would walk by faith in the Word of God, not by my feelings. I would seek to be a Bible Christian. Since that time the Lord has given me a steady victory over sins which before enslaved me. I delight in the Lord, and in His Word. I delight in my work as a minister: my fellowship is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ. I am a baby in Christ; I know my progress has been small compared with that made by many. My feelings vary. But when I feel, I praise God and trust His word. When I'm empty and feel nothing, I do the same. I have covenanted to walk by faith and not by feelings. The Lord is beginning to revive His work among my people. “Praise the Lord.” May the Lord fill you with all His fullness and give you all the mind of Christ. Oh, be faithful! Walk before God and be perfect. Preach the Word. Be instant in season and out of season. The Lord loves you. He works with you. Rest your soul completely upon that promise, “Look, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.” Your fellow soldier, WILLIAM HILL There may be some who will object to this teaching, that it ignores the work of the blessed Holy Spirit. But I must refer such to the introductory chapter of this book, in which I have fully explained myself. I am not writing upon that side of the subject; I am considering man ’s part in the matter, and not the part of the Spirit. I know that all a man can do would be useless if the Holy Spirit did not work in him continually. I write as I do because I believe in the Spirit. It is a mighty, ever-present power, ready to do his work. But, like the wind that blows where it wants, you hear its sound. But you cannot tell where it comes from or where it goes. The Spirit's actions are beyond our control and understanding. The results we know, and the steps on our part which lead to those results, but we know nothing more. And yet, like a factory worker, we dare to urge men to act. They must, like the worker, trust an unseen power, called steam, behind their machinery. It can accomplish the impossible. We know the mighty Spirit will always provide the power needed for each moment's act. We boldly claim that we, as writers, can say, as earnestly as any other Christians, "We believe in the Holy Ghost."

fields.title: Is God In Everything?
fields.body_html:
Recognizing God's presence in all aspects of life, including human actions and trials, is essential. Everything, even suffering caused by others, is part of God's plan and must be accepted as His will. By trusting in His sovereignty, believers can face difficulties with peace, knowing that God oversees all and uses even challenges for spiritual growth and triumph.

Amajor obstacle to living a life of total surrender is the difficulty of seeing God in everything.

People say, "I can submit to things from God. But, I cannot submit to man. "Most of my trials come through humans." Or, "It's fine to talk of trusting. But, when I commit a matter to God, man is sure to come in and mess it up. I can trust God, but I see serious problems with trusting men."”

This is no imaginary trouble. It is of vital importance. If it cannot be met, it makes faith an impossible, visionary theory. Nearly everything in life comes to us through human means. Most of our trials result from someone's failure, ignorance, carelessness, or sin. We know God cannot be the author of these things. Yet, unless He is the agent, how can we say to Him, "Your will be done"? Besides, what good is it to trust our affairs to God, if man can come in and disrupt them? And, how can we live by faith if we can't trust humans? They will have too much influence on our lives.

Moreover, things in which we can see God’s hand always have a sweetness in them which consoles while it wounds. But, man's trials are full of bitterness. So, we must see God in everything. We must accept all things as His direct gifts, with no second causes. We must be brought to this. Only then can we know a lasting experience of total abandonment and perfect trust. Our abandonment must be to God, not to man, and our trust must be in Him, not in any arm of flesh, or we shall fail at the first trial.

The question is, "Is God in everything? “Do we have scripture to accept everything from Him? It was caused by other factors."" I answer, unhesitatingly, yes. To the children of God, all comes from their Fath er's hand. It matters not who the apparent agents were. There are no “second causes” for them. The whole teaching of the Bible asserts and implies this. “Not a sparrow falls to the ground without our Father.” The very hairs of our head are all numbered. We are not to be careful about anything, because our Father cares for us. We are not to avenge ourselves, because our Father has charged Himself with our defence.

We are not to fear, for the Lord is on our side. No one can be against us, because He is for us. We shall not want, for He is our Shepherd. When we pass through the rivers, they shall not overflow us. When we walk through the fire, we shall not be burned. He will be with us. He shuts the mouths of lions, that they cannot hurt us. He delivers and rescues. He changes the times and the seasons; He removes kings and sets up kings. A man’s heart is in His hand, and, as the river of water, He turns it whithersoever He will.” "He rules over all the heathen kingdoms. In His hand is power and might. None can withstand Him."

He rules the raging of the sea; when the waves thereof arise, He stills them. He brings the advice of the unruly to mischief; He makes the devices of the people of no effect. Whatsoever the Lord pleases that does Him in heaven, and in earth, in the seas, and all deep places. If you see the poor oppressed and justice perverted, don't marvel. For there is one higher than the highest. He sees all. These are a part of His ways, but how little a portion is heard of Him? But the thunder of His power, who can understand?”

"Have you not known, have you not heard? The everlasting God, the Lord, the Creator of the ends of the earth, does not grow faint or weary. There is no searching of His understanding.

And this God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear. The earth may be removed. The mountains may be carried into the sea. The waters may roar and be troubled.

The mountains may shake with their swelling. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress, my God, in Him will I trust. Surely He shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noise of some pestilence. He shall cover me with His feathers, and under His wings shall I trust. His truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Do not be afraid of the terror by night, or the arrow that flies by day. Do not fear the pestilence that walks in darkness, or the destruction that wastes at noon.

“A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not c ome near you. You will only look with your eyes and see the recompense of the wicked. Because you have made the Lord your dwelling place, the Most High, who is my refuge, no evil shall be allowed to befall you, no plague come near your tent. For he will co mmand his angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.”

Psalms 91:7-11 These Scriptures, and others like them, settle, once and for all, the question of second causes in the lives of God's children. They are all under the control of our Father. Nothing can touch us except with His knowledge and by His permission. Man's sin may cause the action. So, it can't be called God's will. But by the time it reaches us, it is God's will. We must accept it as directly from His hands.

No man or group, no power on earth or in heaven, can touch the soul that abides in Christ. They must first pass through Him and get His permission. If God be for us, it matters not who may be against us; nothing can disturb or harm us, except He shall see that it is best for us, and shall stand aside to let it pass. An earthly parent’s care for his helpless child is a feeble illustration of this. If the child is in its father’s arms, nothing can touch it without that father’s consent, unless he is too weak to prevent it.

And even if this should be the case, he suffers the harm first in his own person, before he allows it to reach his child. If an earthly parent would thus care for his helpless child, how much more will our Heavenly Father! His love is infinite. His strength and wisdom are unfailing.

Some, even of God's children, doubt His love and care. They secretly blame Him for neglect they would not tolerate. But His care is far beyond human care. He counts the hairs on our heads and knows when a sparrow falls. He watches every small thing that affects His children's lives. He controls them all according to His will, no matter their origin.

The instances of this are numberless. Take Joseph. What could seem more a result of sin than his being sold into slavery? It was u tterly against God's will. And yet Joseph, in speaking of it, said, “ As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive, as they are today. ” Genesis 50:20.Now, do not be grieved or angry with yourselves for selling me. “ God sent me here to preserve life." To the eye of sense, it was surely Joseph's wicked brethren who had sent him into Egypt.

Yet, with faith, Joseph could say, "God sent me." His brothers had sinned. But by the time it reached Joseph, it was God's will. It was, though it didn't seem so at first, the greatest blessing of his life. So we see how the Lord can turn even man's anger to praise Him. And, how all things, even others' sins, shall work for good to those who love Him.

I learned this lesson, practically and experimentally, long before I knew the scripture. I was at a prayer meeting for scriptural holiness. A strange lady rose to speak. I wondered who she was, not knowing she would teach me a grand lesson. She said she had great difficulty in living a life of faith. The second cause that seemed to control everything about her caused it. Her confusion grew. She began to ask God to teach her the truth. Was he really in everything, or not?

After praying this for a few days, she had what she described as a vision. She thought she was in a dark place. Then, a body of light advanced towards her from a distance. It gradually surrounded and enveloped her and everything around her. As it approached, a voice seemed to say, “This is the presence of God; this is the presence of God.” This presence showed her all the great and awful things in life.

She saw fighting armies, wicked men, raging beasts, storms, and plagues. She saw every kind of sin and suffering. At first, she shrank back in terror. But, she soon saw that God's presence surrounded and enveloped each one of these. Not a lion could reach out its paw, nor a bullet fly through the air, except as His presence moved to permit it.

She knew that, if there were the thinnest of sheets of this glorious presence between her and the terrible violence, nothing could touch her. Not a hair on her head could be ruffled.

But, the presence must divide to let the evil through. Then, all the small annoyances of life flashed before her. She saw they were so wrapped in God's presence that nothing could touch her. Not a cross look, harsh word, or petty trial could reach her unless He let them through.

Her difficulty vanished. Her question was answered forever. God was in everything, and to her henceforth there were no second causes. She saw that her life came to her, day by day, and hour by hour, from His hand. It did not matter what seemed to control it. And, she never again found it hard to trust in His care. But if we focus on the seen things, we won't understand this secret. The children of God must "not look at the things which are seen: for the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal." If we could see His unseen forces around us, we'd feel safe. We would walk through this world in an unbreakable fortress. For "the angel of the Lord encamped round about them that fear Him, and delivered them."

We have a striking illustration of this in the history of Elisha. The king of Syria was at war with Israel.

His evil plans were foiled by a prophet. So, he sent his army to the prophet's city to capture him. We read, “He sent their horses and chariots and a great host; and they came by night and compassed the city about.” This was the seen thing. A nd the servant of the prophet, whose eyes had not yet been opened to see the unseen things, was alarmed. We read, "And when the man, God's servant, rose early and went forth, a host encompassed the city, with horses and chariots." His servant said, "Alas, my master, how shall we do?” But his master could see the unseen things, and he replied, “Fear not; for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” And then he prayed, saying, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes that he may see.

The Lord opened the young man's eyes, and he saw. The mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha. The presence of God is the fortress of His people. Nothing can withstand it. At His presence, the wicked perish. The earth trembles. The hills melt like wax. The cities crumble. "The heavens also dropped, and Sinai itself was moved at the presence of God." In this secret, He has promised to hide His people from man's pride and from the strife of tongues. "My presence shall go with thee," He says, "and I will give you rest." I wish every Christian could see this truth as plainly as I do. It is the only clue to a completely restful life. Nothing else will let a soul live only in the present, as we are commanded to do. We must not think of tomorrow.

Nothing else will remove all the risks from a Christian's heart. It won't let him say, "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life." Abiding in God’s presence, we run no risks. A soul like that can say: "I know not what it is to doubt. My heart is always gay. "I run no risks, for, come what will, God always has His way." I once heard of a colored woman. She earned a precarious living by daily labor. But, she was a joyous, triumphant Christian.

“Ah!”Nancy," said a gloomy Christian lady one day. She almost disapproved of her constant cheerfulness, yet envied it.

"Ah!" Nancy, it is all well enough to be happy now, but I should think the thoughts of your future would sober you. Only suppose, for instance, that you fell sick and couldn't work. Or, suppose your employers moved away, and no one else hired you. Or suppose -- "Stop!” cried Nancy, “I never supposes.

The Lord is my shepherd, and I know I shall not want. And, honey,” she added to her gloomy friend, “I know it’s all those things they’re suggesting that are making you so miserable . You should give them all up and just trust in the Lord. ” One text can end a believer's "suppose." If only it is received and acted on with childlike faith. It is in Heb. 3:5- 6 “ Now Moses was f aithful in all God’s house as a servant, to testify to the things that were to be spoken later, but Christ is faithful over God’s house as a son. And we are his house, if indeed we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in our hope . ” Be content with what you have. For He said, “Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, ' I will never leave you nor forsake you.” So we can confidently say, the Lord is my Helper, I will not fear. What can man do to me?” Hebrews 13:5-6 What if dangers threaten you from every side? What if men's malice, foolishness, or ignorance combine to harm you?

You may face every contingency with these words: "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.”

If the Lord is your helper, how can you fear what man may do unto you? No man, nor any company of men, can touch you. Unless, of course, your God, in whom you trust, allows it. “He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep. The Lord is your keeper; the Lord is your shade on your right hand. The sun shall not strike you by day, nor the moon by night. The Lord will keep you from all evil; he will keep your life. The Lord will keep you going out and your coming in from this time forth and forevermore.” (Psalm 121:3 - 8) Only seeing God in everything will make us loving and patient with those who annoy us.

They will be only instruments for His wise, tender purposes. We'll end up thanking them for the blessings they bring. Nothing else will completely put an end to all murmuring or rebellious thoughts.

Christians often feel a liberty to murmur against man when they would not dare to murmur against God. But this way of receiving things would make it impossible ever to murmur. If our Father allows a trial, it must be the best thing for us. We must accept it with thanks from His dear hand.

The trial itself may be hard to flesh out and blood, and I do not mean that we can like or enjoy the suffering of it. But we can and must love the will of God in the trial, for His will is always sweet, whether it be in joy or in sorrow. Our trials may be our chariots. We long for some victory over sin and self, and we ask God to grant it to us.

His answer comes in the form of a trial, which He means shall be the chariot to bear us to the longed for triumph. We may either let it roll over us and crush us like an unstoppable force. Or we may mount into it and ride triumphantly onward. Joseph's chariots, which raised him to glory, were his trials. They were being sold into slavery and unjustly imprisoned.

Our chariots may be less than these. They may be just annoying people or tough situations. But whatever they are, God means them to be our forces of triumph.

They shall bear us to the victories we have prayed for. If we are impatient and long to be patient, our chariot will probably be a trying person. Their ways or words will test our very souls. If we accept the trial as from God and submit, it will be the best discipline. It will give us the patience we seek.

God does not order the wrong thing. But, He uses it for our blessing. He did this with the cruelty of Joseph's wicked brethren. And, with Pharaoh's wife's false accusations. It makes life a long thanksgiving. It gives us a deep peace and a joy beyond words. Someone says, “God’s will on earth is always joy, always tranquility.” He must have His own way with His children. The soul that learns this secret finds green pastures and still waters. They offer rest and refreshment.

If the will of God is our will, and if He always has His way, then we always have our way also, and we reign in a perpetual kingdom. He who sides with God will win every time. Whatever the outcome, we can join the ap ostle's victory shout: “ But their minds were hardened. For to this day, when they read the old covenant, that same veil remains uplifted , because only through Christ is it taken away.”

(2Corinthians 2:14)
