Leave it with the Lord, and remember that what you trust to Him, you must not worry over nor feel anxious about. Trust and worry cannot go together. If your work is a burden, it is because you are not trusting it to Him. If you trust it to Him, you will find the yoke He puts on you is easy. The burden He gives you is light. Even amid a life of ceaseless activity, you will find rest for your soul. But some may say that this teaching would make us into mere puppets. I answer, No, it would simply make us into servants. A servant must not plan, arrange, decide, or supply materials. He must only obey. It is for the Master to do all the rest. The servant is not responsible, either, for results. The Master alone knows what results he wished to have produced, and so he alone can judge of them. Intelligent service must, of course, sympathize with the Master's plans. But, there cannot be a full understanding. The Master cannot shift his responsibility to the servant. With our limited view and great ignorance, we can do little but accept God's will. We shouldn't expect to fully understand it. We must leave all results to Him. What seems like failure on the surface is often, on the unseen side, a great success. If we allow ourselves to lament and worry, we will be foolish. We should be singing and rejoicing, not weeping. It is far better to avoid all self-reflection. We should not think about ourselves at all, whether for good or ill. We are not our own property, nor our own business. We belong to God. We are His instruments and His business. He always attends to His own business. So, He will, of course, attend to us. I once heard of a slave on a ship during a violent storm. While everyone else was scared, he whistled happily. Finally, someone asked if he was afraid of drowning. He smiled and said, "Well, maybe I am. But I don’t belong to myself, and it will only be my master’s loss." This attitude could help us avoid many worries in our work. With a group of people fully dedicated to serving and trusting in our Master, imagine what He could do. One person like this could defeat a thousand, and two could put ten thousand to flight. Nothing would be impossible for them because, with the Lord, it doesn’t matter whether we have many or few. May God quickly raise such an army! And may you, my dear reader, enroll in this army today. Yield yourself to God as one alive from the dead. May every part of you be His instrument of righteousness, to be used by Him as He wishes.

fields.title: Difficulties Concerning Guidance
fields.body_html:
Believers are encouraged to trust in God's promised guidance, despite struggles with doubts about His will. God speaks through Scripture, the Holy Spirit's impressions, personal judgment, and providential circumstances. These must align to confirm His will. The chapter warns against self-deception and stresses testing impressions with Scripture and common sense. Ultimately, believers are urged to trust God’s wisdom and act promptly on His guidance while avoiding doubt.

You have now begun, dear reader, the life of faith. You have given yourself to the Lord, to be His wholly. He has taken you and begun to mold you into a vessel of His honor. Your deepest desire is to be very flexible in His hands. You want to follow Him wherever He may lead you.

You trust Him to work in you to will and to do of His good pleasure. But you find a great difficulty here. You do not know the voice of the Good Shepherd. So, you are in doubt about His will for you.

God is calling you to certain paths. Your friends express strong disapproval. And, these friends may be older than you in the Christian life. They seem much more advanced, too. You can hardly bear to differ from or distress them. You also feel very unsure about yielding to any duty they might disapprove of.

Yet, you cannot shake these impressions. You plunge into doubt and unease. There is a way out of all these difficulties, to the fully surrendered soul. I would repeat, fully surrendered. Any will to resist makes it hard to know God's mind on that point. So, first, ensure you truly want to obey the Lord in all respects. If this is the case, your soul only needs to know God's will to consent to it.

Then, you cannot doubt His desire to make it known and to guide you.

There are many very clear promises in reference to this. Take, for instance, John 10:3- 4 “To him the gatekeeper opens. The sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out, when he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice. ” John 14:26: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you." Also, James 1:56: “If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. ” With such passages as these, and many more like them, we must believe that Divine guidance is promised to us, and our faith must confidently look for and expect it.

This is essential; for in James 1:6- 7, we are told, “ But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord .

First, settle this point. Divine guidance has been promised. You will surely have it if you ask for it.

Let no doubt turn you from this.

Next, remember that our God has all knowledge and wisdom. Therefore, He may guide you to paths where great blessings await you. But, to the short-sighted human eyes around you, those paths may seem to lead to confusion and loss.

You must accept that God's thoughts and ways differ from man’s . Only He, who knows the end from the beginning, can judge the results of any action. You must realize that His love for you may lead you to go against your dearest friends' wishes.

You must learn from Luke 14 and similar passages, “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not bear his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple. For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it? Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish.’ Or what king, going out to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and deliberate whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand? And if not, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace. So therefore, any one of you who does not renounce all that he has cannot be my disciple.” ( Luke 14:26-33.)

To be a disciple of your Lord, you may need to forsake all you have. You may have to turn your back on your family, or even your own life. If this is not clearly recognized, the soul may suffer. Often, a child's path of obedience will displease those he loves most. If he cannot trust the Lord through this, he will be lost.

Of course, this is in harmony with our duties of honor and love to one another in our various life relationships. The closer we are to Christ, the more we will show His meekness and gentleness. We will also be tender to our natural guardians and counselors. The Master's guidance will always show itself by the Master's Spirit. If, in obeying Him, we act against our friends' wishes, our love and patience will prove our motive. But, this point settled, we now ask how God's guidance will come to us. How shall we know His voice?

There are four special ways God speaks: 1. the voice of Scripture, 2. the inward impressions of the Holy Spirit, 3. our higher judgment, and 4. providential circumstances. If these four align, it is safe to say that God speaks. I lay it down as a principle, which none can dispute. His voice will always be in harmony with itself, no matter how many ways He may speak.

The voices may be many, the message can be but one. If God tells me in one voice to do or to leave undone anything, He cannot possibly tell me the opposite in another voice. If there is a contradiction in the voices, the speaker cannot be the same.

My rule for distinguishing the voice of God is to test it against this harmony. If I have an impression, I must check if it aligns with Scripture. I must also see if my higher judgment approves it, and, as we Quakers say, if "way opens" to carry it out. If either test fails, it is not safe to proceed. I must wait in quiet trust until the Lord shows me the point of harmony. He will, if it is His voice that has spoken. For we must not overlook the fact that there are other voices that speak to the soul. There is the loud and clamoring voice of self that is always seeking to be heard. And there are the voices of evil, deceiving spirits. They lie in wait to entrap every traveler who enters these higher regions of the spiritual life.

In the same epistle which tells us that we are seated in “ and raised us up with him and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus , ” (Eph. 2:6) , we are also told that we shall have to fight there with spiritual enemies. “ For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.” (Eph. 6:12). These spiritual enemies, whoever they are, must communicate with us through our spiritual faculties. Their voices, therefore, will be, like God's, an inward impression on our spirits.

So, just as the Holy Spirit may tell us, by impressions, the will of God, so will these spiritual enemies.

They will, by impressions, tell us their will, though not giving their name. It is plain, therefore, that we need a test. We must try these inner impressions. It is to know whose voice is speaking. And that test will always be the harmony to which I have referred. In a misguided attempt to honor the Divine Spirit, some earnest Christians have ignored and even violated the Bible. They have disregarded clear signs from Providence and outraged their own better judgment. God, who sees their sincere hearts, can and does forgive. But, the consequences in this life are often very sad.

We must first test any voice claiming to be divine. It must align morally with God's mind and will, as revealed in the Gospel of Christ. Whatever is contrary to this, cannot be Divine, because God cannot contradict Himself. We cannot expect a direct revelation until we seek and obey God's will, as revealed in the Bible. A great many fatal mistakes are made in this matter of guidance, by the overlooking of this simple rule. If our Father has given us clear directions, He won't reveal anything more. No man needs or could expect a direct revelation to tell him not to steal. God has already, in the Scriptures, plainly declared His will about it. It seems so obvious that I would not mention it. But, I have met Christians who overlooked it and became fanatical.

For the Scriptures are far more explicit even about details than most people think. And there are not many important affairs in life for which a clear direction may not be found in God’s book.

Take the matter of dress, and we have 1 Pet. 3:3- 4 “ Do not let your adorning be external — the braiding of hair and the putting on of gold jewelry, or the clothing you wear — but let your adorning be the hidden person of the heart with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which in God’s sight is very precious .” and 1 Tim. 2:9 - 10 “ likewise also that women should adorn themselves in respectable apparel, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly attire, but with what is proper for women who profess godliness —with good works.”

Take the matter of conversation, and we have Eph. 4:29 “ Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear . ” , and 5:4 “ Let there be no filthiness nor foolish talk nor crude joking, which are out of place, but instead let there be thanksgiving .” Take the matter of avenging injuries and standing up for your rights, and we have (Romans.12:19- 21) “ Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God, for it is written, “Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord.” To the contrary, “if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for by so doing you will hear burning coals on his head.” Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good ,” and (Matthew. 5:38 - 48) “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you, do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well. And if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles. Give to the one who begs from you, and do not refuse the one who would borrow from you. You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”

“ For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For what credit is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God. For to this you have been called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps .”(1Peter.

2:19-21) Take the matter of forgiving one another, and we have (Ephesians.4:32) “ Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.”

Mark 11:25- 26 “And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses .” Take the matter of conformity to the world, and we have (Romans 12:20) “ Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect. ” and (1 John 2:15- 17) “ Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world — the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life — is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever.

“ You adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God?

Therefore, whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.”(James 4:4) Take the matter of anxieties of all kinds, and we have (Matthew 6:25- 34) “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? And which of you, by being anxious, can add a single hour to his span of life?

And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore, do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’

or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all. But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. “Therefore , do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

“ Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.”( Philippians 4:6-7) I only give these as examples to show how very full and practical the Bible guidance is. If you are confused, first, check if the Bible addresses your question. Ask God to reveal His will to you through the Scriptures. And whatever shall seem to you to be plainly taught there, that you must obey. Reading and meditating on this record of God's mind and will enlightens us. The inspiring Spirit will do so. Our obedience will then be, as if, a present, living word. It will be as if our Lord spoke it to us today from Heaven. The Bible is an ancient message from God, sent to us long ago. It is also a present message, sent to us now each time we read it.

"My words are spirit and life. You must obey them. It's a command, personal and present." But we must remember, the Bible is a book of principles. It is not a group of unrelated sayings . Isolated texts may be used to sanction things. These are opposed by Scripture's principles.

I recently heard of a Christian woman at a Western meeting. The text, "For we walk by faith, and not by sight," brought it to mind. She felt it was a command to be literally obeyed. So, she blindfolded herself and insisted on walking up and down the aisle to illustrate the walk of faith. She soon stumbled and fell against the stove, burning herself. Then, she wondered at the mysterious dispensation.

Applying Scripture and her common sense would have saved her from the delusion.

The second test, therefore, is our own higher judgment, or common sense. It is as true now as in Solomon's time. A "man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels." His exhortation still binds us: "Get wisdom, the principal thing. “Wi th all you're getting, get understanding." The Scriptures say it is vital for God's children to use all their abilities on their journey through this world. They are to use their outward faculties for their outward walk, and their inward faculties for their inward walk. They might as well expect to be "kept" from stubbing their toes if they walk blindfolded. It's the same as expecting to be "kept" from spiritual stumbling if they ignore their judgment and common sense.

I asked a "sound mind" Christian how she told false spirits from the Holy Spirit. She replied, "I rap them over the head and see if they have any common sense." Some may say, "But we should not depend on our human understanding in divine things." I answer that we should not depend on our unenlightened understanding. We should rely on our judgment and common sense, which the Spirit of God has enlightened. That is, God will speak to us through the faculties He has Himself given us, and not independently of them. We must use our eyes when we walk, no matter how faithful we are.

Similarly, we must use our minds in our inner lives.

The third and last test is that of providential circumstances. If a “leading” is of God, a way will always open for it. Our Lord assures us of this in John 10:4. It says, “When he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice. ” Notice here the expressions “goes before,” and “ follows .” He goes before to open a way, and we are to follow in the way thus opened. A Christian should not force his way and trample opposition. That is never a sign of a Divine leading. If the Lord “goes before” us, He will open all doors for us, and we shall not need ourselves to hammer them down.

The fourth point is this: We must test our impressions by the other three voices. We must also test those voices by our inward impressions. If we feel a "stop in our minds" about anything, we must wait until it is removed before acting. A Christian, who had quickly advanced in the Divine life, gave me this secret: "I always mind the checks." We must not ignore our inner voice, nor ride roughshod over it, any more than we must the other three voices of which I have spoken.

These four voices, then, will always be found to agree in any truly Divine leading. The voice of our impressions, the voice of Scripture, the voice of our own sanctified judgment. The voice of providential circumstances. If these four do not agree at first, we must wait until they do.

A divine sense of “oughtness,” derived from the harmony of all God’s various voices, is the only safe foundation for any action. I have guarded the points of danger. So, please let me out. I long for the joy of this direct communication of God's will to us. It seems to me to be the grandest of privileges. In the first place, that God should love me enough to care about the details of my life is perfectly wonderful.

And that He would tell me all about it. And, to know how to live and walk to perfectly please Him, seems almost too good to be true.

We never care about the little details of people’s lives unless we love them. We don't care what most people do or how they spend their time. But when we love someone, we start to care. God's care for us proves His love. It's a great blessing that He speaks to us about everything in our lives. This includes our duties, pleasures, friendships, and all we do, think, or say.

You must know this in your own experience, dear reader. Only then will you find the joy and privilege of a life hid with Christ in God. It is one of its most precious gifts. God promises to work in us to will and to do of His good pleasure.

This means He will take control of our will and work it for us. His suggestions will come to us as desires, not commands. They will originate in our will; we shall feel as though we wanted to do so and so, not as though we must. This makes it a service of perfect liberty. For it is always easy to do what we desire, no matter how difficult the circumstances. Every mother knows she could get perfect obedience from her child. She just needs to control his will, making him want to do what she wants.

And this is what our Father does for His children in the new dispensation.

He writes His laws on our hearts and minds. We love them. Our affections and judgment, not our fears, draw us to obey. The Holy Spirit usually guides by impressing a desire to do or avoid certain things.

In prayer, the soul feels a sudden suggestion about a duty. “I would like to do this or the other,” it thinks, “I wish I could.” Or the suggestion may come as a question, “I wonder whether I had not better do so and so?” Or it may be only at first in the way of a conviction that such is the right and best thing to be done. The matter should be committed to the Lord. We must instantly choose to obey Him. If the suggestion agrees with the Scriptures, a holy judgment, and the circumstances, we should obey it.

Immediate obedience is the safest and easiest course. When the Spirit speaks, it is easy to obey. But if the soul hesitates and reasons, it becomes harder to obey.

The first convictions are usually right in a fully surrendered heart. God is faithful and will make His voice heard above all others. Such convictions, therefore, should never be met by reasoning. Prayer and trust are the only safe attitudes of the soul. But even these should be brief.

We must act before the time passes and we miss the blessing.

If the suggestion is unclear and doubt arises, we should wait for further insight. This is especially true if our friends disagree. The Scripture rule is, “Whatsoever is not of faith is sin” which means plainly that we must never act in doubt. A clear conviction of right is the only safe guide. But we must wait in faith. We must fully surrender, saying, "Yes," to our Lord's will, whatever it may be.

Our troubles stem from a lack of will. Next, many doubt any real Divine guidance. God's children are very skeptical here. They read the promises and feel the need. But, they cannot believe that someone will guide them.

It's as if God wants us to obey His voice, but didn't know how to make us hear and understand Him. It is, thus, very possible for God to speak, but for the soul not to hear, because it does not believe He is speaking. No earthly parent or master could guide his children or servants if they did not believe him or accept his voice as his true will. God, who spoke to the fathers in many ways, still speaks. He wants to see if any souls will obey His will.

Every moment of our lives our Father is seeking to reveal Himself to us. “ Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am he.”(John 4:26) I that speak in your heart, in your circumstances, in your losses, in your gains, in your sorrows, and in your joys, am He. "I speak everywhere and in everything." So, we must have perfect faith that the Lord's voice is speaking to us. It will teach and lead us. He will give us wisdom for our guidance. After asking for guidance, we must follow our strongest sense of what we should do. A few rules can help us with this.

I. We must believe that God will guide us.

II. We must surrender our own will to His guidance.

III. We must hearken for the Divine voice.

IV. We must wait for the divine harmony.

When we are certain of God’s guidance, we must follow it without hesitation. He is our t rue home. The path may be difficult and narrow, but nothing else can satisfy a heart that longs for Him. How little of that path you have walked, my soul! Take courage, and let the thought of God draw you further. The perfect way may be hard for the flesh, but it is not hard for love. If you were desperate for God, how quickly you would move toward Him.

Do not give your duties to God reluctantly — let your hands be open and free. Fix your eyes on Jesus and consider how freely He gave His love to you. True perfection requires only a heart that remains at peace throughout the day, listening for the Spirit’s voice moment by moment. Keep your conscience sensitive — do not ignore His quiet nudges. And go wherever His grace leads you.
fields.body_text: Believers are encouraged to trust in God's promised guidance, despite struggles with doubts about His will. God speaks through Scripture, the Holy Spirit's impressions, personal judgment, and providential circumstances. These must align to confirm His will. The chapter warns against self-deception and stresses testing impressions with Scripture and common sense. Ultimately, believers are urged to trust God’s wisdom and act promptly on His guidance while avoiding doubt. You have now begun, dear reader, the life of faith. You have given yourself to the Lord, to be His wholly. He has taken you and begun to mold you into a vessel of His honor. Your deepest desire is to be very flexible in His hands. You want to follow Him wherever He may lead you. You trust Him to work in you to will and to do of His good pleasure. But you find a great difficulty here. You do not know the voice of the Good Shepherd. So, you are in doubt about His will for you. God is calling you to certain paths. Your friends express strong disapproval. And, these friends may be older than you in the Christian life. They seem much more advanced, too. You can hardly bear to differ from or distress them. You also feel very unsure about yielding to any duty they might disapprove of. Yet, you cannot shake these impressions. You plunge into doubt and unease. There is a way out of all these difficulties, to the fully surrendered soul. I would repeat, fully surrendered. Any will to resist makes it hard to know God's mind on that point. So, first, ensure you truly want to obey the Lord in all respects. If this is the case, your soul only needs to know God's will to consent to it. Then, you cannot doubt His desire to make it known and to guide you. There are many very clear promises in reference to this. Take, for instance, John 10:3- 4 “To him the gatekeeper opens. The sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out, when he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice. ” John 14:26: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you." Also, James 1:56: “If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. ” With such passages as these, and many more like them, we must believe that Divine guidance is promised to us, and our faith must confidently look for and expect it. This is essential; for in James 1:6- 7, we are told, “ But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord . First, settle this point. Divine guidance has been promised. You will surely have it if you ask for it. Let no doubt turn you from this. Next, remember that our God has all knowledge and wisdom. Therefore, He may guide you to paths where great blessings await you. But, to the short-sighted human eyes around you, those paths may seem to lead to confusion and loss. You must accept that God's thoughts and ways differ from man’s . Only He, who knows the end from the beginning, can judge the results of any action. You must realize that His love for you may lead you to go against your dearest friends' wishes. You must learn from Luke 14 and similar passages, “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not bear his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple. For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it? Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish.’ Or what king, going out to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and deliberate whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand? And if not, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace. So therefore, any one of you who does not renounce all that he has cannot be my disciple.” ( Luke 14:26-33.) To be a disciple of your Lord, you may need to forsake all you have. You may have to turn your back on your family, or even your own life. If this is not clearly recognized, the soul may suffer. Often, a child's path of obedience will displease those he loves most. If he cannot trust the Lord through this, he will be lost. Of course, this is in harmony with our duties of honor and love to one another in our various life relationships. The closer we are to Christ, the more we will show His meekness and gentleness. We will also be tender to our natural guardians and counselors. The Master's guidance will always show itself by the Master's Spirit. If, in obeying Him, we act against our friends' wishes, our love and patience will prove our motive. But, this point settled, we now ask how God's guidance will come to us. How shall we know His voice? There are four special ways God speaks: 1. the voice of Scripture, 2. the inward impressions of the Holy Spirit, 3. our higher judgment, and 4. providential circumstances. If these four align, it is safe to say that God speaks. I lay it down as a principle, which none can dispute. His voice will always be in harmony with itself, no matter how many ways He may speak. The voices may be many, the message can be but one. If God tells me in one voice to do or to leave undone anything, He cannot possibly tell me the opposite in another voice. If there is a contradiction in the voices, the speaker cannot be the same. My rule for distinguishing the voice of God is to test it against this harmony. If I have an impression, I must check if it aligns with Scripture. I must also see if my higher judgment approves it, and, as we Quakers say, if "way opens" to carry it out. If either test fails, it is not safe to proceed. I must wait in quiet trust until the Lord shows me the point of harmony. He will, if it is His voice that has spoken. For we must not overlook the fact that there are other voices that speak to the soul. There is the loud and clamoring voice of self that is always seeking to be heard. And there are the voices of evil, deceiving spirits. They lie in wait to entrap every traveler who enters these higher regions of the spiritual life. In the same epistle which tells us that we are seated in “ and raised us up with him and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus , ” (Eph. 2:6) , we are also told that we shall have to fight there with spiritual enemies. “ For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.” (Eph. 6:12). These spiritual enemies, whoever they are, must communicate with us through our spiritual faculties. Their voices, therefore, will be, like God's, an inward impression on our spirits. So, just as the Holy Spirit may tell us, by impressions, the will of God, so will these spiritual enemies. They will, by impressions, tell us their will, though not giving their name. It is plain, therefore, that we need a test. We must try these inner impressions. It is to know whose voice is speaking. And that test will always be the harmony to which I have referred. In a misguided attempt to honor the Divine Spirit, some earnest Christians have ignored and even violated the Bible. They have disregarded clear signs from Providence and outraged their own better judgment. God, who sees their sincere hearts, can and does forgive. But, the consequences in this life are often very sad. We must first test any voice claiming to be divine. It must align morally with God's mind and will, as revealed in the Gospel of Christ. Whatever is contrary to this, cannot be Divine, because God cannot contradict Himself. We cannot expect a direct revelation until we seek and obey God's will, as revealed in the Bible. A great many fatal mistakes are made in this matter of guidance, by the overlooking of this simple rule. If our Father has given us clear directions, He won't reveal anything more. No man needs or could expect a direct revelation to tell him not to steal. God has already, in the Scriptures, plainly declared His will about it. It seems so obvious that I would not mention it. But, I have met Christians who overlooked it and became fanatical. For the Scriptures are far more explicit even about details than most people think. And there are not many important affairs in life for which a clear direction may not be found in God’s book. Take the matter of dress, and we have 1 Pet. 3:3- 4 “ Do not let your adorning be external — the braiding of hair and the putting on of gold jewelry, or the clothing you wear — but let your adorning be the hidden person of the heart with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which in God’s sight is very precious .” and 1 Tim. 2:9 - 10 “ likewise also that women should adorn themselves in respectable apparel, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly attire, but with what is proper for women who profess godliness —with good works.” Take the matter of conversation, and we have Eph. 4:29 “ Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear . ” , and 5:4 “ Let there be no filthiness nor foolish talk nor crude joking, which are out of place, but instead let there be thanksgiving .” Take the matter of avenging injuries and standing up for your rights, and we have (Romans.12:19- 21) “ Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God, for it is written, “Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord.” To the contrary, “if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for by so doing you will hear burning coals on his head.” Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good ,” and (Matthew. 5:38 - 48) “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you, do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well. And if anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles. Give to the one who begs from you, and do not refuse the one who would borrow from you. You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” “ For this is a gracious thing, when, mindful of God, one endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For what credit is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if when you do good and suffer for it you endure, this is a gracious thing in the sight of God. For to this you have been called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in his steps .”(1Peter. 2:19-21) Take the matter of forgiving one another, and we have (Ephesians.4:32) “ Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.” Mark 11:25- 26 “And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses .” Take the matter of conformity to the world, and we have (Romans 12:20) “ Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect. ” and (1 John 2:15- 17) “ Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world — the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life — is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever. “ You adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore, whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.”(James 4:4) Take the matter of anxieties of all kinds, and we have (Matthew 6:25- 34) “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what you will put on. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. He wants to see if any souls will obey His will. Every moment of our lives our Father is seeking to reveal Himself to us. “ Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am he.”(John 4:26) I that speak in your heart, in your circumstances, in your losses, in your gains, in your sorrows, and in your joys, am He. "I speak everywhere and in everything." So, we must have perfect faith that the Lord's voice is speaking to us. It will teach and lead us. He will give us wisdom for our guidance. After asking for guidance, we must follow our strongest sense of what we should do. A few rules can help us with this. I. We must believe that God will guide us. II. We must surrender our own will to His guidance. III. We must hearken for the Divine voice. IV. We must wait for the divine harmony. When we are certain of God’s guidance, we must follow it without hesitation. He is our t rue home. The path may be difficult and narrow, but nothing else can satisfy a heart that longs for Him. How little of that path you have walked, my soul! Take courage, and let the thought of God draw you further. The perfect way may be hard for the flesh, but it is not hard for love. If you were desperate for God, how quickly you would move toward Him. Do not give your duties to God reluctantly — let your hands be open and free. Fix your eyes on Jesus and consider how freely He gave His love to you. True perfection requires only a heart that remains at peace throughout the day, listening for the Spirit’s voice moment by moment. Keep your conscience sensitive — do not ignore His quiet nudges. And go wherever His grace leads you.

fields.title: Concerning Temptation
fields.body_html:
Temptation is not a sign of failure but a part of spiritual growth. It’s not a sin to be tempted, only to yield to it. Discouragement is a trap, and trusting God with temptation strengthens faith. Enduring temptation leads to spiritual growth and the "crown of life" promised to those who persevere.

Some very big mistakes are made about temptation in this life of faith. First, people expect that, after the soul rests in God, temptations will cease. They believe the promised salvation is from both temptation and being tempted. When they find the Canaanite still in the land, and see the great, walled cities, they are discouraged. They think they must have gone wrong and that this cannot be the true land after all.

Next, they mistakenly see temptation as sin. They blame themselves for it, but it's the enemy's fault.

This leads to condemnation and discouragement. If it continues, it ends in sin. The enemy makes an easy prey of a discouraged soul; so that we fall often from the very fear of having fallen. To solve the first difficulty, I must refer to Scripture. It says the Christian life is a constant warfare. It also says we must, especially when seated in heavenly places in Christ Jesus, wrestle against spiritual enemies there.

Their power and skill to tempt us must be far superior to any we've ever encountered.

Temptations usually grow tenfold in strength after we start the interior life, not decrease. Their power must not lead us to doubt that we have found the true, abiding place. Strong temptations are generally a sign of great grace, rather than of little grace. When the Israelites first left Egypt, the Lord did not lead them through the Philistines' land, the nearest route. God said, “When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near. For God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.” But, when they learned to trust Him, He allowed their enemies to attack. In their wilderness journey, they met few enemies and fought few battles. In the land, they faced seven great nations and thirty-one kings. They had to conquer walled cities and defeat giants.

They could not have fought the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites until they had entered their land. Your temptations, dear Christian, may prove you are in the land you seek to enter. They are unique to that land. Never let your temptations make you doubt that you are in the promised "heavenly places."

The second mistake is not quite so easy to deal with. It's almost pointless to say that temptation is not sin. Yet, most distress comes from not understanding this. The very suggestion of wrong seems to bring pollution with it. The evil agency not recognized, the poor, tempted soul fears it must be very bad, and far from God, to have had such thoughts. It is as though a burglar broke into a man's house to steal.

When the owner began to resist him, the burglar accused him of being the thief. It is the enemy's clever trick to trap us.

He comes and whispers evil ideas to us: doubts, blasphemies, jealousy, envy, and pride. Then he says, "Oh, how wicked you must be to think of such things!" It is plain that you do not trust the Lord. If you did, these things would not have entered your heart. This reasoning seems true, so the soul accepts it.

It then feels condemned and discouraged. From there, it is easy to fall into sin. One of the most fatal things in the life of faith is discouragement.

One of the most helpful is cheerfulness. A wise man once said that, in overcoming temptations, cheerfulness was the key. It was the first, second, and third thing. We must expect to conquer. That is why the Lord often told Joshua, “Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go ” (Joshua 1:9). And it is also the reason He says to us, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid” (John14:27) .

The power of temptation is in the fainting of our own hearts. The enemy knows this. He always tries to discourage us at the start of his assaults, if he can.

Sometimes, we feel discouraged. We think it's righteous grief and disgust at ourselves for being tempted. But it's really an embarrassment . We are ashamed because we secretly congratulated ourselves. We believed our tastes were too pure and our separation from the world too complete for such things to tempt us. We expected something from ourselves. We are disappointed to find it lacking.

As a result, we are discouraged. This embarrassment and discouragement are worse than the temptation. They seem humble, but they only stem from wounded self-love.

True humility can bear to see its own weakness and foolishness revealed. It never expected anything from itself. It knows its only hope must be in God. So, instead of discouraging the soul from trusting, it drives it to a deeper and more utter trust. But counterfeit humility, born of self, plunges the soul into despair. It drives it into the very sin it so despises. I remember once hearing an allegory that illustrated this to me wonderfully. Satan called together a council of his servants to consult how they might make a good man sin. One evil spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.” “How will you do it?” asked Satan. “I will set before him the pleasures of sin,” was the reply; “I will tell him of its delights and the ri ch rewards it brings.” “Ah,” said Satan, “that will not do; he has tried, it, and knows better than that.”

Then another spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.”

“What will you do?” asked Satan. “I will tell him of the pains and sorrows of v irtue. I will show him that virtue has no delights, and brings no rewards.” “Ah, no!” exclaimed Satan, “That will not do at all.

He has tried it. He knows, 'wisdom's ways are pleasant, and her paths are peace.' Another said, I will make him sin. And what will you do? Asked Satan, again. I will discourage his soul, was the short reply. Ah, that will do,” cried Satan, “that will do! We shall conquer him now.” And they did. An old writer says, all discouragement is from the devil. I wish every Christian would remember this and keep it as a pocket-piece. We must fly from discouragement as we would from sin. But this is impossible if we fail to recognize the true agency in temptation. For if the temptations are our own fault, we cannot help being discouraged. But they are not.

The Bible says, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him. ”(James 1:12) It urges us to "count it all joy when we fall into diverse temptations." Temptation, therefore, cannot be sin. It is no more a sin to hear evil whispers in our souls than to hear the swearing of bad men as we pass along the street. The sin only comes in either case by our stopping and joining in with them. If, when the wicked thoughts come, we turn from them at once, as we would from wicked talk, and ignore them, we do not sin. But if we carry them on in our minds, and roll them under our tongues, and dwell on them with a half consent of our will to them as true, then we sin.

We may be enticed by evil a thousand times a day without sin, and we cannot help these enticing. But if the enemy can make us think his temptations are our sin, he will have won half the battle. He will then likely win completely.

A dear lady once came to me under great darkness, simply from not understanding this. She had been very happy in her faith for some time. She had been free from temptation, and thought she would never be tempted again. But suddenly a very peculiar form of temptation had assailed her, which had horrified her. She found that the moment she began to pray, dreadful thoughts of all kinds would rush into her mind. She had lived a very sheltered, innocent life. These thoughts seemed so awful to her, that she felt she must be one of the wicked of sinners to have them. She began by thinking she could not have entered into the rest of faith. She ended by concluding that she had never been born again.

Her soul was in an agony of distress.

I told her that these dreadful thoughts were the enemy's doing. He came to her the moment she kneeled in prayer and filled her mind with them. She was not to blame for them at all. She could not help them any more than she could help hearing a wicked man blaspheme in her presence. I urged her to see them as from the enemy. She should not blame or discourage herself. Instead, she should turn to Jesus and commit them to Him. I showed her how much the enemy had gained. They made her think these thoughts were her own. This condemned and discouraged her. I assured her she would win quickly if she ignored them. She should turn her back on them and look to the Lord.

She grasped the truth, and the next time these thoughts came she said to the enemy, “I have found you out now. It is you who are suggesting these dreadful thoughts to me, and I hate them, and will have nothing to do with them. The Lord is my Saviour; take them to Him, and settle them in His presence.”

The baffled enemy, found out, fled in confusion. Her soul was perfectly delivered.

Another thing also. The enemy knows that if a Christian sees a hint of evil as his, he will reject it. He will do so more quickly than if it seems to be his own mind's suggestion. If Satan began each temptation with, "I am Satan, your enemy; I have come to make you sin," we would likely resist. He has to hide himself in order to make his baits attractive. Our victory will be easier if we are not ignorant of his tricks. We must recognize him at his first approach. We also make a mistake about temptations. We think that all time spent fighting them is wasted. Hours pass, and we seem to have made no progress, because we have been so beset with temptations. But, we may have served God more truly during these hours than in our freer times, when we faced fewer temptations.

Temptation is really more the devil’s wrath against God, than against us. He cannot touch our Saviour.

But, he can wound Him by conquering us. Our ruin matters to him only as it does this. So, we fight our Lord's battles when we resist temptation. In these cases, an hour is worth a day's time. We read, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him ."(James 1:12).I am sure this means to endure its continuance and frequent recurrence.

Nothing cultivates the grace of patience like enduring temptation. And, nothing drives the soul to depend on the Lord Jesus like it. And finally, nothing brings more glory to our Lord than the trial of our faith, which comes through many temptations. It is said to be more precious than gold, though tested by fire. We, who endure the trial, shall receive a reward. It is "the crown of life" which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.”

We cannot wonder at the Holy Ghost's urging at the start of the Book of James: " Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness. And let steadfastness have its full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing. ”(James 1:2)Temptation is God's tool to complete our perfection. So, the enemy's own weapons are turned against him. We see that all things, even temptations, can work for good to them that love God.

To resist temptations, I don’t need to tell my audience: it is by faith. For this is, of course, the foundation upon which the whole interior life rests. Our one great motto is throughout, “We are nothing, and Christ is all.” A nd always and everywhere we have started to stand, and walk, and overcome, and live by faith. We have found our own helplessness. We cannot help ourselves. Our only way, therefore, is to hand the temptation over to our Lord and trust Him to conquer it for us.

But when we put it into His hands, we must leave it there. We must commit to Him for victory as we did for salvation. He must do all for us in the one case, as completely as in the other. It was faith only then, and it must be faith only now.

The Lord works miracles in conquering the temptations of those who trust Him. Thousands can testify to this. But I cannot expand on this now. I aimed to show temptation in its true light, not to detail the way to overcome it. I want to free good, faithful souls from bondage. They will be trapped if they confuse temptation with sin. They must understand temptation's true nature and use. I want them to know that temptations are vital for our souls' growth. Whatever their source, God uses them to build in us graces of character that would otherwise be missing.

Wherever temptation is, there is God also, superintending and controlling its power. “Where were you, Lord I, while I was being tempted?” cried the saint of the desert. "Close beside you, my son, all the while," was the tender reply. Temptations try us. We are worth nothing if we are not tried. They develop our spiritual strength and courage and knowledge, and our development is the one thing God cries for.

How shallow would all our spirituality be if it were not for temptations? "Blessed is the man who endures temptation. He will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love Him." This "crown of life" will be worth all the trials and endurance it costs to obtain it; without those, it could not be attained.

A sick woman once bought a cocoon . It held a very beautiful butterfly with magnificent wings. She hoped to see it emerge from the cocoon in her chamber. She watched it eagerly as spring drew on.

Finally, she was delighted to see the butterfly beginning to emerge. But it seemed to have great difficulty. It pushed, and strained, and struggled. It made so little headway that she concluded it must need help. With a pair of delicate scissors, she clipped the tight cord that bound the cocoon's opening.

Immediately the cocoon opened wide, and the butterfly escaped without any further struggle. She congratulated herself on her experiment's success. But, something was wrong with the butterfly.

It was all out of the cocoon, it's true. But, its great wings were lifeless and colorless. They dragged behind it, a useless burden. For a few days it lived a miserable sickly life, and then died, without having once lifted its powerless wings. The lady was sorely disappointed and could not understand it. But when she related the circumstance to a naturalist, he told her that it had all been her own fault. That it took just that pushing and struggling to send the life fluid into the wings' veins. Her misguided kindness in shortening the struggle had left the wings lifeless and colorless.

So, our spiritual wings need the struggle of resisting temptation. To save us from it would weaken our souls' power to "mount up with wings as eagles." It would also deny us the "crown of life" promised to those who endure.

fields.title: Failures
fields.body_html:
Failures in the Christian life are inevitable but should not lead to despair. When we sin, immediate confession and trust in God’s forgiveness restore our fellowship with Him. Hidden sin can cause spiritual defeat, and we must deal with it honestly. Failures should drive us closer to God, not away, and through His grace, we continue walking in holiness.

The very title of this chapter may startle some. “Failures,” they will say; “we thought t here were no failures in this life of faith!” To this I would answer that there ought not to be, and need not be; but, as a fact, there sometimes are. And we have got to deal with facts, and not with theories. No teacher of this inner life says we can't sin. They only insist that we don't have to. A chance for constant victory is now possible. Few deny that, at times, they have given in to temptation.

Of course, in speaking of sin here, I mean conscious, known sin. I do not touch on the sins of ignorance.

Nor do I discuss the so-called inevitable sin of our nature. Both are covered by the atonement and do not disturb our fellowship with God. I have no desire or ability to discuss the doctrines of sin. I will leave that to the theologians. I will speak only of the believer's experience. I want it to be clear that I will refer only to what is within our consciousness. Misunderstanding, then, on this point of known sin, is dangerous to the higher Christian life. A believer, who trusts he is on the highway of holiness, may be surprised into sin. The highway of holiness is not a place, but a way. Sanctification is not a thing to be gained at a certain stage of our experience and forever possessed. It is a life to be lived day by day and hour by hour.

We may briefly stray from a path. But our wandering does not erase it. We can quickly return. In this life of faith, we may fail at times. These failures are sad and to be deplored. But, if met rightly, they need not disturb our complete trust in God. They should not interrupt our happy communion with Him for long.

No matter the cause of our failure, discouragement won't help. A child learning to walk might despair after a fall. He might refuse to try again. A believer, learning to live by faith, must not give up for having sinned. The only way in both cases is to get right up and try again. After a disastrous defeat.

“Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of the Lord until the evening, he and the elders of Israel. And they put dust on their heads. And Joshua said, "Alas, O Lord God, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? Would that we had been content to dwell beyond the Jordan! O Lord, what can I say when Israel has turned their backs before their enemies? For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and will surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?"(Joshua 7:6-9) What a wail of despair this was! And how it is repeated by many a child of God today. Their hearts melt, like water, because of a defeat. They cry, “And Joshua said, 'Alas, Lord G OD , why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all — to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us?

Oh, that we had been content, and dwelt on the other side of the Jordan !" They predict further failures and even defeat by their enemies. No doubt, Joshua thought, as we now do. After such a failure, discouragement and despair seemed the only safe response. But God thought otherwise. " So the L ORD said to Joshua: “Get up! Why do you lie thus on your face? " They should not surrender to despair, however humble it might seem. They must face the evil and get rid of it. They must "sanctify themselves" at once.”

“Up, sanctify the people,” is always God’s command. “Lie down and be discouraged” is always the enemy’s temptation. We feel it is presumptuous, even impertinent, to go at once to the Lord after having sinned against Him. We should suffer our sins' consequences for a while and endure our guilty consciences. We can hardly believe the Lord would want to welcome us back into His loving fellowship. A little girl once expressed the feeling to me, with a child's honest straightforwardness. She asked if the Lord Jesus always forgave our sins if we asked Him. I said, "Yes, of course He does."”

“Just as soon” she repeated, doubtingly. “Yes,” I replied, “the very minute we ask, He forgives us.”

“Well,” she said deliberately, “I cannot believe that. I should think He would make us feel sorry for two or three days first. And then I should think He would make us ask Him a great many times, and in a very pretty way too, not just in common talk. I believe that is how He does. You need not try to make me think He forgives me at once, no matter what the Bible says.”

She only said what most Christians think. Worse, most act on it. Their remorse now separates them from God more than their sin would.

It is so contrary to how we want our children to act, that I wonder how we could have conceived such an idea of God. A mother grieves when her naughty child goes off alone in despair. She doubts her willingness to forgive. But, her heart welcomes the darling who runs to her and begs forgiveness!

Surely, our God knew this love when He said, “ Return, O faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness.

Behold, we come to you, for you are the Lord our Go d.”(Jeremiah3:22) The same moment that reveals sin, should reveal forgiveness. This is vital for a steadfast walk on the holy path. Here, we cannot tolerate an instant of separation from God. We can only walk this path by looking to Jesus, moment by moment. If we take our eyes off Him to see our sin and weakness, we will leave the path at once. The believer, who trusts he is on this path, must flee to the Lord if sin overcomes him. He must act on ( 1 John 1:9) “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and j ust to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” He must not hide his sin and seek to salve it over with excuses, or to push it out of his memory by the lapse of time. But he must do as the children of Israel did. He must rise up "early in the morning," and "run" to where the evil thing is hidden. Then, he must take it from its hiding place and lay it "out before the Lord.”

He must confess his sin. Then he must stone it, burn it, and put it away. Then, he must raise a great heap of stones to hide it forever. He must, then and there, believe that God is. He must believe, according to His word, that God is faithful and just to forgive him his sin, and that He does do it. He must also believe that God cleanses him from all unrighteousness. He must, by faith, claim an immediate forgiveness and cleansing. Then, he must trust more than ever.

Once Israel's sin was uncovered and removed, God's word came. It was a message of great encouragement: " And the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take all the fighting men with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, and his people, his city, and his land. ”(Joshua 8:1) Our courage must rise higher than ever. We must trust the Lord more. Then, His mighty power can work in us to fulfill His will. Moreover, we must forget our sin as soon as it is thus confessed and forgiven. We must not dwell on it, and examine it, and indulge in a luxury of distress and remorse. We must not idolize it, then walk around and view it. That would make it a mountain that hides our God from us. We must follow Paul's example. We must "forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before." Then, we must "press toward the ma rk for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."”

I would like to bring up two contrastive illustrations of these things. One was an earnest Christian. He was an active church worker. For several months, he had enjoyed full salvation. He was suddenly overcome by a temptation to treat a brother unkindly. He thought it impossible to sin again. So, he was deeply discouraged. He concluded he was wrong. He had never truly trusted. His discouragement grew into despair. He concluded he had never been born again, and gave himself up for lost. He spent three years in misery. He drifted further from God and fell into one sin after another. His life became a curse to himself and to those around him.

His health failed under the terrible burden. Fears arose for his reason. At the end of three years, he met a Christian lady, who understood the truth about sin that I had been trying to explain. After a brief chat, she learned his trouble. She said, "You sinned in that act, no doubt. Don't try to excuse it."

But have you never confessed it to the Lord and asked Him to forgive you?” “Confessed it!” He exclaimed, "I have done nothing but confess it. I have begged God to forgive me for these three dreadful years." “And you have never believed He did forgive you?” asked the lady. “No,” said the poor man, “how could I, for I never felt as if He did?” “But suppose He had said He forgave you, would not that have done as well as for you to feel it?”

“Oh, yes,” replied the man, “if God said it, of course I would believe it.” “Very well, He does say so,” was the lady’s answer, and she turned to the verse we have taken above. “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness . ”(1 John 1:9) and read it aloud. "Now," she continued, "for three years you've confessed your sin. All the while, God's record has declared He is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse you. Yet, you have never once believed it."

You have been ‘making God a liar’ all this while by refusing to believe His record.”

The poor man saw the whole thing. He was dumbfounded and alarmed. When the lady suggested they kneel, he obeyed like one in a maze. She wanted him to confess his past sins and claim, then and there, forgiveness and cleansing. But the result was glorious. In a few moments, the light broke in, and he burst out into praise at the wonderful deliverance. In three minutes, his soul, by faith, traversed the long, weary journey of three years. He found himself resting in Jesus, rejoicing in His full salvation.

The other illustration was of a Christian lady. She had been in salvation for about two weeks. She had a bright, victorious experience. Suddenly, at the end of that time, she was overcome by a violent burst of anger. For a moment, a flood of discouragement swept over her soul. The enemy said, “There, now, that shows it was all a mistake. Of course, you have been deceived about the whole thing, and have never entered into the life of full trust at all.

You might as well give up. You can't consecrate or trust yourself more than you did this time. So, it is plain this life of holiness is not for you!” These thoughts flashed through her mind in a moment. But she was well-taught in God's ways. So, she said, "Yes, I have sinned, and it is very sad." But the Bible says that if we confess our sins, God will forgive us. He is faithful and just. He will also cleanse us from all unrighteousness. I believe He will do it.” She did not delay. Still boiling with anger, she ran, not walked, into a room to be alone. Kneeling by the bed, she said, "Lord, I confess my sin." I have sinned, I am even at this very moment sinning.

I hate it, but I cannot get rid of it. I confess it with shame and confusion of face to God. And now I believe that, according to your word, you do forgive and you do cleanse.” She said it out loud, for the inward turmoil was too great for it to be said inside. As the words “You do forgive and you do cleanse” passed her lips, the deliverance came. The Lord said, “ And he awoke and rebuked the wind and said to the sea , ' Peace! Be still!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm ,” ( Mark 4:39) and there was a great calm. A flood of light and joy burst on her soul, the enemy fled, and she was more than a conqueror through Him that loved her. It had taken only five minutes, the sin and its cure. Now, her feet trod more firmly than ever on the blessed highway of holiness. So, the valley of anchor became a door of hope. She sang her song of deliverance, with deeper m eaning: “Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, 'I will sing to the LORD, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1 ) In every crisis, the only remedy is to trust in the Lord. If this is all we can do, is it not better to do it at once? I have often been brought up short by the question, “Well, what can I do but trust?” I realized at once the folly of seeking deliverance any other way. I thought, "I will have to trus t in the end. “Then, why not do it now?" We have entered a life of faith. If we fail, our only recovery must be an increase in faith, not a decrease.

Let every failure, if any occur, drive you to the Lord. Abandon yourself to Him and trust Him completely. Though sad, these failures won't end your rest or your sweet communion with Him. I have shown the way to escape failure. Now, I want to discuss the causes of failure in this life of full salvation.

The causes do not lie in the strength of the temptation, our own weakness, or, above all, any lack in our Saviour's power or will to save us. The promise to Israel was positive, “ No man shall be able to stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not leave you or forsake you. ” (Joshua1:5). And the promise to us is equally positive, " No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation he will also provide a way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.” 1 Corinthians 10:13) So about three thousand men went up there from the people. And they fled before the men of Ai It was not the strength of their enemy, neither had God failed them. Their defeat had another cause, which the Lord declares: "Israel hath sinned. They have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them.

They have taken of the accursed thing. They have also stolen and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff."

"So, the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies. They turned their backs upon their enemies."” It was a hidden evil that conquered them. Deep beneath the earth, in a tent in that vast army, was something against which God had a controversy.

This hid den thing made the whole army helpless before their enemies. “Israel, there is something wrong among you . You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove it."”

The teaching is this: Any hidden evil in our hearts, no matter how small, will cause us to fall before our enemies. Any cherished bitterness, harsh judgments, or slackness in obeying the Lord will cripple our spiritual life. So will any doubtful habits or surroundings. We may have hidden the evil in our hearts.

We may have covered it up, refusing to see it. But, we are secretly aware of it.

We may ignore it and declare our full trust. We may be more earnest in our religious duties. We may see more truth and beauty in the life of faith. We may seem to have won, both to ourselves and others.

Yet, we may suffer bitter defeats. We may wonder, question, despair, and pray. But, nothing will help until the accursed thing is dug up, brought to light, and laid before God. If a believer living an inner life is defeated, he must seek the cause. It is not the enemy's strength. It is a hidden lack of dedication at his core.

A headache is not a disease, but a symptom of one. It is in some other part of the body. So, in a Christian, sin is only a symptom. It reveals an evil that likely exists in another part of his being.

Sometimes, one may hide evil even in what, at a cursory glance, looks like good. Hidden behind a strong desire for the truth, there may be a tendency to judge or favor our own opinions . Clear Christian faithfulness may hide an absence of Christian love. Beneath a seemingly rightful care for our affairs, we may hide a great want of trust in God. Our blessed Guide, the indwelling Holy Spirit, is. He secretly discovers these things to us. He does so through little twinges and pangs of conscience. So, we are left without excuse. It is easy to ignore His gentle voice. We convince ourselves that all is well. This will hide a fatal evil among us, causing unexpected defeats.

A capital illustration of this occurred to me once in my housekeeping. I moved into a new house. In checking it for readiness, I found a very clean cider cask in the cellar. It was headed up at both ends. I debated whether to take it from the cellar and open it. It seemed empty and looked nice. So, I decided to leave it, as it would have been a lot of work to get it up the stairs. I didn't feel completely comfortable, but I pushed aside my doubts and left it. Every spring and fall, during house-cleaning time, I would remember that cask. A twinge of my housewifely conscience nagged at me. I could not rest in a perfectly cleaned house while it remained unopened. For how did I know it did not hide some evil beneath its fair exterior?

Still, I eased my doubts. I feared the trouble of investigating it. For two or three years, the harmless- looking barrel sat in my basement. Then, most unaccountably, moths began to fill my house. I used every possible precaution against them and made every effort to eradicate them, but in vain. They increased rapidly and threatened to ruin everything I had.

I suspected my carpets were the cause, and subjected them to a thorough cleaning. I suspected something was wrong with my furniture, so I had it redone. I suspected all sorts of impossible things.

At last, the thought of the cask flashed on me. I had it brought up from the cellar, and the head knocked in.

I think it's safe to say that thousands of moths poured out. The previous occupant must have left something that bred moths. This was the cause of all my trouble.

I now believe that some habit or indulgence, some safe, minor thing, causes us little twinges of conscience. It's not been fairly examined under God's searching eye. I think it lies at the root of most failures in this higher life. All is not given up. Some secret corner is kept locked against the entrance of the Lord. And therefore, we cannot stand before our enemies, but find ourselves smitten down in their presence.

To prevent failure, or to find its cause if we do, we must keep this prayer before us: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me and know my thoughts; and see if there be any evil way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.""

There may be something very deceptive in our sufferings over our failures. We may think we are focused on God's glory. Yet, our souls may be troubled by self alone. We are not as saintly as we thought. This discovery hurts our self-love. Our frustration can be a bigger mistake than the original wrongdoing. The only safe way to treat our failures is to avoid justifying or condemning ourselves.

We should, instead, lay them quietly before the Lord. We should look at them in peace and with love.

The old mystic writers say that a simple, peaceful turning to God helps us more than regretting our straying from Him. "Only be faithful," they say. "Turn only to Him, the moment you see your sin. His presence will free you from the snares that have trapped you." To look at self-plunges you deeper into the slough, for this very slough is after all nothing but self; while a simple look towards God can calm and comfort your heart.

Finally, let us never forget, no matter our failures. The Lord Jesus is able, as declared, to save us from our enemies. Then, we may "That we, being delivered from the hand of our enemies, might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days."(Luke1:74-75). Let us pray, each of us, day and night: " Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me .”(Psalm19:13). “ But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”(Acts 1:8). We must be so pliable in His hands, and trust Him. Then He will “ Equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.” (Hebrews 13:21)
