And now I believe that, according to your word, you do forgive and you do cleanse.” She said it out loud, for the inward turmoil was too great for it to be said inside. As the words “You do forgive and you do cleanse” passed her lips, the deliverance came. The Lord said, “ And he awoke and rebuked the wind and said to the sea , ' Peace! Be still!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm ,” ( Mark 4:39) and there was a great calm. A flood of light and joy burst on her soul, the enemy fled, and she was more than a conqueror through Him that loved her. It had taken only five minutes, the sin and its cure. Now, her feet trod more firmly than ever on the blessed highway of holiness. So, the valley of anchor became a door of hope. She sang her song of deliverance, with deeper m eaning: “Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, 'I will sing to the LORD, for he has triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1 ) In every crisis, the only remedy is to trust in the Lord. If this is all we can do, is it not better to do it at once? I have often been brought up short by the question, “Well, what can I do but trust?” I realized at once the folly of seeking deliverance any other way. I thought, "I will have to trus t in the end. “Then, why not do it now?" We have entered a life of faith. If we fail, our only recovery must be an increase in faith, not a decrease. Let every failure, if any occur, drive you to the Lord. Abandon yourself to Him and trust Him completely. Though sad, these failures won't end your rest or your sweet communion with Him. I have shown the way to escape failure. Now, I want to discuss the causes of failure in this life of full salvation. The causes do not lie in the strength of the temptation, our own weakness, or, above all, any lack in our Saviour's power or will to save us. The promise to Israel was positive, “ No man shall be able to stand before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not leave you or forsake you. ” (Joshua1:5). And the promise to us is equally positive, " No temptation has overtaken you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation he will also provide a way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.” 1 Corinthians 10:13) So about three thousand men went up there from the people. And they fled before the men of Ai It was not the strength of their enemy, neither had God failed them. Their defeat had another cause, which the Lord declares: "Israel hath sinned. They have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them. They have taken of the accursed thing. They have also stolen and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff." "So, the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies. They turned their backs upon their enemies."” It was a hidden evil that conquered them. Deep beneath the earth, in a tent in that vast army, was something against which God had a controversy. This hid den thing made the whole army helpless before their enemies. “Israel, there is something wrong among you . You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove it."” The teaching is this: Any hidden evil in our hearts, no matter how small, will cause us to fall before our enemies. Any cherished bitterness, harsh judgments, or slackness in obeying the Lord will cripple our spiritual life. So will any doubtful habits or surroundings. We may have hidden the evil in our hearts. We may have covered it up, refusing to see it. But, we are secretly aware of it. We may ignore it and declare our full trust. We may be more earnest in our religious duties. We may see more truth and beauty in the life of faith. We may seem to have won, both to ourselves and others. Yet, we may suffer bitter defeats. We may wonder, question, despair, and pray. But, nothing will help until the accursed thing is dug up, brought to light, and laid before God. If a believer living an inner life is defeated, he must seek the cause. It is not the enemy's strength. It is a hidden lack of dedication at his core. A headache is not a disease, but a symptom of one. It is in some other part of the body. So, in a Christian, sin is only a symptom. It reveals an evil that likely exists in another part of his being. Sometimes, one may hide evil even in what, at a cursory glance, looks like good. Hidden behind a strong desire for the truth, there may be a tendency to judge or favor our own opinions . Clear Christian faithfulness may hide an absence of Christian love. Beneath a seemingly rightful care for our affairs, we may hide a great want of trust in God. Our blessed Guide, the indwelling Holy Spirit, is. He secretly discovers these things to us. He does so through little twinges and pangs of conscience. So, we are left without excuse. It is easy to ignore His gentle voice. We convince ourselves that all is well. This will hide a fatal evil among us, causing unexpected defeats. A capital illustration of this occurred to me once in my housekeeping. I moved into a new house. In checking it for readiness, I found a very clean cider cask in the cellar. It was headed up at both ends. I debated whether to take it from the cellar and open it. It seemed empty and looked nice. So, I decided to leave it, as it would have been a lot of work to get it up the stairs. I didn't feel completely comfortable, but I pushed aside my doubts and left it. Every spring and fall, during house-cleaning time, I would remember that cask. A twinge of my housewifely conscience nagged at me. I could not rest in a perfectly cleaned house while it remained unopened. For how did I know it did not hide some evil beneath its fair exterior? Still, I eased my doubts. I feared the trouble of investigating it. For two or three years, the harmless- looking barrel sat in my basement. Then, most unaccountably, moths began to fill my house. I used every possible precaution against them and made every effort to eradicate them, but in vain. They increased rapidly and threatened to ruin everything I had. I suspected my carpets were the cause, and subjected them to a thorough cleaning. I suspected something was wrong with my furniture, so I had it redone. I suspected all sorts of impossible things. At last, the thought of the cask flashed on me. I had it brought up from the cellar, and the head knocked in. I think it's safe to say that thousands of moths poured out. The previous occupant must have left something that bred moths. This was the cause of all my trouble. I now believe that some habit or indulgence, some safe, minor thing, causes us little twinges of conscience. It's not been fairly examined under God's searching eye. I think it lies at the root of most failures in this higher life. All is not given up. Some secret corner is kept locked against the entrance of the Lord. And therefore, we cannot stand before our enemies, but find ourselves smitten down in their presence. To prevent failure, or to find its cause if we do, we must keep this prayer before us: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me and know my thoughts; and see if there be any evil way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting."" There may be something very deceptive in our sufferings over our failures. We may think we are focused on God's glory. Yet, our souls may be troubled by self alone. We are not as saintly as we thought. This discovery hurts our self-love. Our frustration can be a bigger mistake than the original wrongdoing. The only safe way to treat our failures is to avoid justifying or condemning ourselves. We should, instead, lay them quietly before the Lord. We should look at them in peace and with love. The old mystic writers say that a simple, peaceful turning to God helps us more than regretting our straying from Him. "Only be faithful," they say. "Turn only to Him, the moment you see your sin. His presence will free you from the snares that have trapped you." To look at self-plunges you deeper into the slough, for this very slough is after all nothing but self; while a simple look towards God can calm and comfort your heart. Finally, let us never forget, no matter our failures. The Lord Jesus is able, as declared, to save us from our enemies. Then, we may "That we, being delivered from the hand of our enemies, might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days."(Luke1:74-75). Let us pray, each of us, day and night: " Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me .”(Psalm19:13). “ But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”(Acts 1:8). We must be so pliable in His hands, and trust Him. Then He will “ Equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.” (Hebrews 13:21)

fields.title: Doubts
fields.body_html:
Christians often struggle with doubts that hinder their faith. Doubt is seen as a sinful habit that must be rejected, just like other temptations. Overcoming it requires fully surrendering to God, trusting in His promises, and refusing to entertain doubts. A life of continuous trust in God’s love and faithfulness is essential.

Agreat number of Christians are slaves to the habit of doubting. No drunkard was ever more completely bound by the chains of his fatal habit than they are by those chains. Their whole Christian life is a constant battle. An army of doubts lies in wait to attack at any chance. Their lives are wretched. Their doubts hinder their usefulness and break their communion with God.

The soul's entry into the life of faith, which this book discusses, often banishes doubts. But, they sometimes resurge. They can cause stumbling and despair. They can't fully turn the believer back to the dreary wilderness.

We all remember, doubtless, the childish mix of fascination and horror in that story. It was about Christian's imprisonment in Doubting Castle by the wicked giant Despair. We felt extremely happy in his escape from those massive gates and that cruel tyrant. We did not suspect then that we would be imprisoned by the same giant, in the same castle. And yet I fear to every member of the Church of Christ there has been at least one such experience. If it's not fresh in your minds, please read the account again. You may find there experiences of your own. They were very hard to bear and sorrowful to remember.

It's strange that people called Believers must confess such doubts. Their name suggests their only trait is belief. It is such a universal habit that, if the Church were renamed, "Doubters" would be the only fitting name. Most Christians have accepted their doubts. They see them as a painful, inevitable illness.

They must resign themselves to it as part of life's discipline. They complain about their doubts as a man might complain about his aches and pains. They want to be seen as an "interesting case" of rare trial, needing deep sympathy and great care.

This is often true of believers. They long to live by faith and have taken many steps towards it. They may have lost their old doubts. They once tormented them. They wondered if their sins were forgiven and if they'd reach Heaven. But, they still doubt. They have simply shifted the habit to a higher platform. They are saying, perhaps, “Yes, I believe my sins are forgiven, and I am a child of God through faith in Jesus Christ. I dare not doubt this anymore.

But then, and this "but then" includes doubts about every promise our Father has made to His children.

They fight with them, refusing to believe until they have better proof of their truth than God's word.

They wonder why they can walk in such darkness. They see themselves as martyrs. They groan under the unique spiritual conflicts they must endure. Spiritual conflicts! Far better would they be named did we call them spiritual rebellions! Our fight is to be a fight of faith, and the moment we doubt, our fight ceases and our rebellion begins.

I desire to put forth, if possible, one vigorous protest against this whole thing. I might as well join in with a drunkard's complaints. I might as well pray with him for grace to endure his fatal indulgence. It is as foolish as to console the enslaved souls with their weak complaints. I can do nothing else but proclaim to them the perfect deliverance the Lord Jesus Christ has for them. I implore, entreat, and command them, with all my being, to accept it and be free. Not for one moment would I listen to their despairing excuses. You ought to be free, you can be free, and you must be free!

Will you undertake to tell me that it is an inevitable necessity for God to be doubted by His children?

Is it an inevitable necessity for your children to doubt you? Would you tolerate their doubts a single hour? Would you pity your son if he said, "Father, I cannot believe your word, I cannot trust your love"? Would you find him an interesting case? I remember once seeing the indignation of a mother I knew, stirred to its very depths by a little doubting on the part of one of her children. She had brought two little girls to my house to leave them while she did some errands. One of them, with a child's happy confidence, abandoned herself to my nursery. She found all the pleasures there. She sang and played until her mother returned.

The other one, with unfortunate caution of maturity, sat alone in a corner. She wondered if her mother would remember to come back for her. She feared being forgotten. She imagined her mother would be glad to get rid of her, since she was a naughty girl. In the end, she worked herself into a perfect frenzy of despair. I shall not easily forget the look on that mother's face. It was after her weeping little girl returned and told her what the matter was. Grief, wounded love, indignation, and pity, all strove together for mastery. But indignation gained the day, and I doubt if that little girl was ever so vigorously dealt with before. That scene has come before me a hundred times since. It has taught me deeply. It has compelled me to refuse doubts about my Heavenly Father's love. Those doubts have clamored at my heart's door for entrance.

I am convinced that, for many, doubting is a luxury. To deny themselves that would be the hardest self- denial they know. It is a luxury that, like all other luxuries, brings sorrowful results. Perhaps, seeing the sadness it has caused in your own Christian life, you may be tempted to say, Sad! This is no luxury to me, but only a fearful trial.” But pause for a moment. Try gi ving it up, and you will soon find out whether it is a luxury or not. Don't your doubts come to you like a group of friends? They sympathize with your troubles and want to comfort you.

Is it not a luxury to sit with them, entertain them, and listen to their arguments? To join in their condolences? Would it be no self-denial to turn resolutely from them, and refuse to hear a word they have to say?

If you don't know, try it and see. Have you never enjoyed the luxury of hard thoughts against those who wronged you? Have you never known the joy of brooding over their unkindness? Of prying into their malice? Of imagining all sorts of wrong, uncomfortable things about them? It has made you wretched, of course. But, it is a fascinating sort of wretchedness that you cannot easily give up. And just like this is the luxury of doubting. Things have gone wrong with you in your experience.

Dispensations are mysterious. Temptations are odd. Your case seems unique. What could be more natural than to conclude that, for some reason, God has forsaken you? That he does not love you and is indifferent to your welfare? And how strong is the belief that you are too wicked for Him to care, or too difficult for Him to manage?

You do not blame Him or accuse Him of injustice. You feel that you deserve His indifference and rejection due to your unworthiness. This trick lets you doubt yourself while pretending to be humble.

But you are indulging in hard, wrong thoughts about your Lord, as much as you did of a human enemy.

He says He came not to save the righteous, but sinners. Your sinfulness and unworthiness are your best claims to His love and care.

The poor little lamb that has wandered and got lost in the wilderness might well say, "The shepherd does not love, care for, or remember me, because I am lost." He only loves and cares for the lambs that never wander.” As well might the ill man say, “The doctor will not come to see me, nor give me any medicines, because I am ill. He only cares for and visits well people.” Jesus say s , “ Those who are well do not need a physician, but those who are sick.”(Mathew 9:12) And again He says, “What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country, and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it? And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”(Luke15:4 -6) Any thoughts of Him that differ from His own words are hard thoughts. To indulge in them is far worse than to indulge in hard thoughts of any earthly friend or foe. From the beginning to the end of your Christian life it is always sinful to indulge in doubts. Doubts are all from the devil, and are always untrue. And the only way to meet them is by a direct and emphatic denial. And this brings me to the practical part of the whole subject, as to how to get deliverance from this fatal habit. My answer would be that the deliverance from this can be by no other means than the deliverance from any other sin. It is to be found in the Lord and in Him only. You must hand your doubting over to Him, as you have learned to hand your other temptations. You must do just what you do with your temper, or your pride.

You must give it up to the Lord.

I believe the only remedy is to take a pledge against it. As you would urge a drunkard to do against drink. Trust in the Lord alone to keep you steadfast.

Like any other sin, the stronghold is in the will. You must surrender your will to doubt, just as you would to any other temptation. God always takes possession of a surrendered will. If we say we will not doubt and surrender our core to Him, His Spirit will work in us. We shall be kept from doubting by His great power. The trouble is, the soul often does not fully surrender. It reserves a small freedom to doubt, seeing it as sometimes necessary. "I do not want to doubt anymore," we will say, or, "I hope I shall not." But , it is hard to say, "I will not doubt again."”

But no surrender is effectual until it reaches the point of saying, “I will not”. The liberty to doubt must be given up forever. And the soul must consent to a continuous life of inevitable trust. I think, it is often necessary to end this doubt. We must reach a decision on it. I believe it is quite as necessary in the case of a doubter as in the case of a drunkard. It will not do to give it up by degrees. The total abstinence principle is the only effectual one here. Once surrendered, the soul must rest entirely on the Lord for deliverance in every temptation. It must lift up the shield of faith the moment the assault comes. It must hand the very first suggestion of doubt over to the Lord, and must tell the enemy to settle the matter with Him.

It must refuse to listen to the doubt a single moment. No matter how plausible or humble it seems, the soul must say, "I dare not doubt; I must trust." The Lord is good, and HE DOES love me. Jesus saves me; He save s me now.” Those three little words, repeated over and over, -- "Jesus saves me, Jesus saves me," -- will defeat the greatest army of doubts that ever attacked a soul. I have tried it times without number, and have never known it to fail. Do not stop to argue the matter out with your doubts, nor try to prove that they are wrong. Pay no attention to them whatever; treat them with the utmost contempt. Shut your door in their faces, and emphatically deny every word they say to you. Bring up some “It is written,” and hurl it after them. Look right at Jesus, and tell Him you trust Him, and you mean to trust Him. Let the doubts clamor as they may, they cannot hurt you if you will not let them in.

It may seem like you are shutting the door on your best friends. Your heart will long for your doubts more than the Israelites longed for the flesh-pots of Egypt. But deny yourself; take up your cross in this matter. Unmercifully refuse to listen to a word. A perfect army of doubts awaited my waking and clamored at my door for admittance. Nothing seemed real or true. Least of all, it seemed possible that I -- miserable and wretched -- could be the object of the Lord's love, care, or notice. If only I could let these doubts in. If I could invite them to sit and make themselves at home, what a luxury that would be! But years ago, I pledged against doubting. I would as soon violate my pledge against liquor as this one.

I dared not admit the first doubt. I lifted my shield of faith the moment I noticed these thoughts. I gave my whole army to my Lord to conquer. Then, I kept saying, "The Lord does love me." He is my present and my perfect Saviour; Jesus saves me, Jesus saves me now!”

The victory was complete. The enemy came in like a flood. But the Lord raised a standard against him.

He was routed and put to flight. My soul sings the song of Moses and the children of Israel. It says, " Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, I will sing to the LORD, FOR he has triumphed gloriously; the hor se and his rider he has thrown into the sea.” (Exodus 15:1) “The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him, my father’s God, and I will exalt him. The Lord is a man of war; the Lord is his name. ”(Exodus 15:2 -3). It will help you to resist the assaults of this temptation to doubt, to see clearly that doubting is sin. It directly disobeys our Lord, who commands us, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid” (John 14:27) The Bible everywhere commands us to trust, with no exceptions. Time and room would fail me to refer to one hundredth part of these. But no one can read the Psalms without being convinced. The man who trusts without question is the only one who pleases and is accepted by God. The “provocation” of Israel was that they did not trust; “Yet they sinned still more against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert. They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved. They spoke against God, saying, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness? He struck the rock so that water gushed out and streams overflowed. Can he also give bread or provide meat for his people? “Therefore, when the Lord heard, he was full of wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob; his anger rose against Israel, because they did not believe in God and did not trust his saving power.” (Psalms 78:17 -22.)

In contrast, Isaiah says of those who tr ust, “You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you. "(Isaiah 26:3) Nothing wounds us like a friend's doubt. I am convinced, nothing grieves God more than our doubt.

One of my children, now with the Lord, said to me one evening as I tucked her in bed, "Well, mother, I have had my first doubt."” “Oh, Ray,” I said, “What was it?” “Why,” she replied, “Satan came to me and told me not to believe the Bible, for it was not a word of it true.” “And what did you say to him?”

I asked. “Oh,” she replied, triumphantly, “I just said to him, Satan, I will believe it. So there!” I was delighted with the child's spiritual intelligence. She knew how to meet doubts. I encouraged her, explaining that all doubts and discouragements are from the enemy. He is a liar, so never listen to him.

The next night, I had forgotten all about it. So, I was surprised when she said, as I tucked her in, "Well, mother, Satan has been at it again."” “Oh, Ray darling!” I exclaimed in dismay, “what did he say this time?” "Well," she replied, "he just told me I was such a naughty girl that Jesus could not love me. It was foolish to think He did."” “And what did you say this time?” I asked. “Oh!” she replied, “I just looked at him cross and said, Satan, shut your mouth!” And then she added, with a smile, “He can’t make me unhappy one bit.” A grander battle no soul ever fought than this little child had done, and no greater victory was ever won!

Dear, doubting soul, go and do likewise; and a similar victory shall be yours. As you lay down this book take up your pen and write out your determination never to doubt again. Make it a real transaction between your soul and the Lord. Give up your liberty to doubt forever. Put your will in this matter over on the Lo rd’s side, and trust Him to keep you from falling. Tell him of your weakness and your doubts.

Your enemy has you helpless. Commit the whole battle to Him. Tell Him you will not doubt again.

Then, keep your gaze on Jesus.

Turn away from yourself and your doubts. Hold on to your faith, for He is faithful who has promised.

If you stay confident to the end, you will, through Him who loves you, be more than a conqueror in this matter.

He only cares for and visits well people.” Jesus say s , “ Those who are well do not need a physician, but those who are sick.”(Mathew 9:12) And again He says, “What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country, and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it? And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”(Luke15:4 -6) Any thoughts of Him that differ from His own words are hard thoughts. To indulge in them is far worse than to indulge in hard thoughts of any earthly friend or foe. From the beginning to the end of your Christian life it is always sinful to indulge in doubts. Doubts are all from the devil, and are always untrue. And the only way to meet them is by a direct and emphatic denial. And this brings me to the practical part of the whole subject, as to how to get deliverance from this fatal habit. My answer would be that the deliverance from this can be by no other means than the deliverance from any other sin. It is to be found in the Lord and in Him only. You must hand your doubting over to Him, as you have learned to hand your other temptations. You must do just what you do with your temper, or your pride. You must give it up to the Lord. I believe the only remedy is to take a pledge against it. As you would urge a drunkard to do against drink. Trust in the Lord alone to keep you steadfast. Like any other sin, the stronghold is in the will. You must surrender your will to doubt, just as you would to any other temptation. God always takes possession of a surrendered will. If we say we will not doubt and surrender our core to Him, His Spirit will work in us. We shall be kept from doubting by His great power. The trouble is, the soul often does not fully surrender. It reserves a small freedom to doubt, seeing it as sometimes necessary. "I do not want to doubt anymore," we will say, or, "I hope I shall not." But , it is hard to say, "I will not doubt again."” But no surrender is effectual until it reaches the point of saying, “I will not”. The liberty to doubt must be given up forever. And the soul must consent to a continuous life of inevitable trust. I think, it is often necessary to end this doubt. We must reach a decision on it. I believe it is quite as necessary in the case of a doubter as in the case of a drunkard. It will not do to give it up by degrees. The total abstinence principle is the only effectual one here. Once surrendered, the soul must rest entirely on the Lord for deliverance in every temptation. It must lift up the shield of faith the moment the assault comes. It must hand the very first suggestion of doubt over to the Lord, and must tell the enemy to settle the matter with Him. It must refuse to listen to the doubt a single moment. No matter how plausible or humble it seems, the soul must say, "I dare not doubt; I must trust." The Lord is good, and HE DOES love me. Jesus saves me; He save s me now.” Those three little words, repeated over and over, -- "Jesus saves me, Jesus saves me," -- will defeat the greatest army of doubts that ever attacked a soul. I have tried it times without number, and have never known it to fail. Do not stop to argue the matter out with your doubts, nor try to prove that they are wrong. Pay no attention to them whatever; treat them with the utmost contempt. Shut your door in their faces, and emphatically deny every word they say to you. Bring up some “It is written,” and hurl it after them. Look right at Jesus, and tell Him you trust Him, and you mean to trust Him. Let the doubts clamor as they may, they cannot hurt you if you will not let them in. It may seem like you are shutting the door on your best friends. Your heart will long for your doubts more than the Israelites longed for the flesh-pots of Egypt. But deny yourself; take up your cross in this matter. Unmercifully refuse to listen to a word. A perfect army of doubts awaited my waking and clamored at my door for admittance. Nothing seemed real or true. Least of all, it seemed possible that I -- miserable and wretched -- could be the object of the Lord's love, care, or notice. If only I could let these doubts in. If I could invite them to sit and make themselves at home, what a luxury that would be! But years ago, I pledged against doubting. I would as soon violate my pledge against liquor as this one. I dared not admit the first doubt. I lifted my shield of faith the moment I noticed these thoughts. I gave my whole army to my Lord to conquer. Then, I kept saying, "The Lord does love me." He is my present and my perfect Saviour; Jesus saves me, Jesus saves me now!” The victory was complete. The enemy came in like a flood. But the Lord raised a standard against him. He was routed and put to flight. My soul sings the song of Moses and the children of Israel. It says, " Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, I will sing to the LORD, FOR he has triumphed gloriously; the hor se and his rider he has thrown into the sea.” (Exodus 15:1) “The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him, my father’s God, and I will exalt him. The Lord is a man of war; the Lord is his name. ”(Exodus 15:2 -3). It will help you to resist the assaults of this temptation to doubt, to see clearly that doubting is sin. It directly disobeys our Lord, who commands us, “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid” (John 14:27) The Bible everywhere commands us to trust, with no exceptions. Time and room would fail me to refer to one hundredth part of these. But no one can read the Psalms without being convinced. The man who trusts without question is the only one who pleases and is accepted by God. The “provocation” of Israel was that they did not trust; “Yet they sinned still more against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert. They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved. They spoke against God, saying, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness? He struck the rock so that water gushed out and streams overflowed. Can he also give bread or provide meat for his people? “Therefore, when the Lord heard, he was full of wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob; his anger rose against Israel, because they did not believe in God and did not trust his saving power.” (Psalms 78:17 -22.) In contrast, Isaiah says of those who tr ust, “You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you. "(Isaiah 26:3) Nothing wounds us like a friend's doubt. I am convinced, nothing grieves God more than our doubt. One of my children, now with the Lord, said to me one evening as I tucked her in bed, "Well, mother, I have had my first doubt."” “Oh, Ray,” I said, “What was it?” “Why,” she replied, “Satan came to me and told me not to believe the Bible, for it was not a word of it true.” “And what did you say to him?” I asked. “Oh,” she replied, triumphantly, “I just said to him, Satan, I will believe it. So there!” I was delighted with the child's spiritual intelligence. She knew how to meet doubts. I encouraged her, explaining that all doubts and discouragements are from the enemy. He is a liar, so never listen to him. The next night, I had forgotten all about it. So, I was surprised when she said, as I tucked her in, "Well, mother, Satan has been at it again."” “Oh, Ray darling!” I exclaimed in dismay, “what did he say this time?” "Well," she replied, "he just told me I was such a naughty girl that Jesus could not love me. It was foolish to think He did."” “And what did you say this time?” I asked. “Oh!” she replied, “I just looked at him cross and said, Satan, shut your mouth!” And then she added, with a smile, “He can’t make me unhappy one bit.” A grander battle no soul ever fought than this little child had done, and no greater victory was ever won! Dear, doubting soul, go and do likewise; and a similar victory shall be yours. As you lay down this book take up your pen and write out your determination never to doubt again. Make it a real transaction between your soul and the Lord. Give up your liberty to doubt forever. Put your will in this matter over on the Lo rd’s side, and trust Him to keep you from falling. Tell him of your weakness and your doubts. Your enemy has you helpless. Commit the whole battle to Him. Tell Him you will not doubt again. Then, keep your gaze on Jesus. Turn away from yourself and your doubts. Hold on to your faith, for He is faithful who has promised. If you stay confident to the end, you will, through Him who loves you, be more than a conqueror in this matter.

fields.title: Practical Results
fields.body_html:
True Christian faith is demonstrated through actions reflecting Christ's holiness.

Believers are called to live humbly, forgive others, and serve God, avoiding worldly pursuits. By surrendering to God’s guidance, Christians grow in Christlikeness, becoming a testimony to His transformative power and love.

If all that has been said about the life hid with Christ in God is true, it should show in our daily lives.

Those who enjoy it should be a "peculiar people, zealous of good works." My son at college once wrote to a friend that Christians must be God's witnesses. The world won't read the Bible, but they will read our lives. Their belief in our religion depends on the report our lives give. As we all know, this is an age of facts. Inquiries are shifting from theories to realities.

If our religion is to make any headway, it must be proved to be more than a theory. We must show, to our age's critical minds, the grand facts of lives transformed by God's mighty power working in us to do His will. "Show us 'forms of life,' say the scientists, and we will be convinced. When the Church presents to them, in all its members, a holy life, their last stronghold will be conquered." I wish, before closing my book, to speak very solemnly of the fruits of a life of faith, such as I have been describing.

I believe they are necessary. I urge my readers to feel their duty to walk worthy of their high calling.

I would speak to some of you, as personal friends. I am sure that, through this book, a mutual longing has grown in your hearts, as it has in mine. We should show forth the praises of Him who has called us out of darkness into His marvellous light. As a friend, I may speak plainly to friends. Please pardon me if I discuss some vital details of life and character. They are important for true Christian growth.

The standard of holy living among Christians is low. Any real devotion in life and walk surprises, and often disapproves, many in the Church. Most professed followers of the Lord Jesus Christ are unlike Him. An outside observer would see little harmony between them.

But we, who have heard God's call to total devotion and trust, must do differently. We must come out from the world and be separate, and must not be conformed to it in our characters nor in our purposes.

We must no longer share in its spirit or its ways.

Our talk must be in Heaven. We must seek things above, where Christ sits at God's right hand. We must walk through the world as Christ walked. We must have the mind that was in Him.

As pilgrims and strangers we must abstain from fleshly lusts that war against the soul. As good soldiers of Jesus Christ, we must avoid the world's affairs as much as possible. This is to please Him who chose us to be soldiers.

We must abstain from all appearance of evil. We must be kind and forgiving to each other. God, for Christ's sake, has forgiven us. We must not resent injuries or unkindness. Instead, we should return good for evil and turn the other cheek to those who hurt us. We must take always the lowest place among our fellowmen; and seek not our own honor, but the honor of others. We must be gentle, and meek, and yielding; not standing up for our own rights, but for the rights of others. All that we do must be done for the glory of God. In summary, since He who called us is holy, we must be holy in our behavior. It is written, "Be you holy, for I am holy."”

Now, dear friends, this is all very practical. It surely means a life very different from most professors' lives. It means that we do really and absolutely turn our backs on self, and on self’s motives and self’s aims. We are a peculiar people, both to God and the world. Our Christ like lives and words will show that we follow the Lord Jesus Christ. We are not of the world, even as He was not of the world. We shall no longer feel that our money is our own, but the Lord’s, to be used in His service. We cannot use our energies only to seek worldly things. If we first seek God's kingdom and His righteousness, we will have what we need.

We will be forbidden to seek high places or worldly gains. We shall not be permitted to be conformed to the world in our ways of thinking or of living. We will have no desire to take part in the world's silly distractions. We should love heavenly things, not earthly ones. We will not serve ourselves, but our Lord. We will perform our duties better than ever. We will work "not with eye service as men pleasers, but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart."”

Clear standard of Christian life, we may not recognize His voice due to ignorance. So, I want to be very plain and definite in my statements. I have noticed that, where there is a faithful following of the Lord in a consecrated soul, several things follow, sooner or later. Over time, meekness and quietness of spirit become the daily life. There is a submissive acceptance of God's will, as it comes in the daily events.

There is also a pliability in God's hands to do or suffer His will. Next, there should be sweetness under provocation, calmness amid chaos, and yieldingness to others' wishes. There is an insensibility to slights and an absence of worry. Fear and care vanish. All these, and many other similar graces, are the natural result of that inward life which is hid with Christ in God.

As for their habits: We always see such Christians, sooner or later, giving themselves to some work for God and their fellowmen. They are willing to spend and be spent in the Master’s service. They become indifferent to their houses' furniture and their living style. They make all personal adornment secondary to the things of God.

The voice is dedicated to God, to talk and sing for Him. The purse is placed at His disposal. The pen is dedicated to write for Him, the lips to speak for Him, the hands and the feet to do His bidding. Year after year, such Christians grow more unworldly and heavenly-minded. They become more like Christ.

Their faces show a beautiful, divine life within them. All who look at them know they live with and abide in God.

I am sure you have each felt some Divine hints. They foreshadow the life I now describe. Have you not begun to feel, deep in your soul, the voice of God speaking to you about these things? Has it not been a pain and a distress to you of late to discover how much is wrong in your life? Hasn't your soul been troubled by doubt about some habits you once indulged in? Have you not begun to feel uneasy with some habits? Do you wish you could change them? Have not paths of devotedness and of service begun to open out before you, with the longing thought, “Oh that I could walk in them”?

All your longings, doubts, and distress are the Good Shepherd's voice. It seeks to call you away from all that is against His will. Oh! Let me entreat you not to turn away from His gentle pleadings. You little know the secret paths He means to lead you to by these very steps. You don't know the great blessings that lie at their end. If you did, you would eagerly obey all His requirements. You can reach the heights of Christian perfection. To do so, you must follow the Guide who will lead you there. He reveals your way one step at a time, through your daily life. He asks only that you yield to His guidance.

If you are convinced of any sin, it is the voice of your Lord. Surrender it at once to His bidding.

Rejoice that He has begun to lead and guide you.

Be completely soft in His wise hands. Go where He entices you. Turn away from all that makes you shrink. Obey Him perfectly. He will lead you swiftly and easily to a wonderful life of conformity to Himself. It will be a testimony to all around you, beyond what you will ever know.

I knew a soul who surrendered to follow the Lord wherever He led her. In three months, she went from deep despair to a blessed union with the Lord Jesus Christ.

In her darkness, she consecrated herself to the Lord. She surrendered her will to Him. She wanted Him to work in her, to do His good pleasure. He began to speak to her by His Spirit in her heart. He suggested small acts of service for Him. He called her away from all un-Christ ways.

She recognized His voice. She feared only disobeying Him. So, she followed Him, yielding to each of His requests, wherever He led her. He led her on, day by day. He conformed her to His will. Her life became a testimony to those around her. Even some who opposed and disbelieved were forced to admit that it was of God. They were won to a similar surrender.

After three short months of this faithful following, it came to pass. So swiftly had she gone that her Lord was able to reveal some of His deepest secrets of love to her wondering soul? He fulfilled the promise of ( Acts 1:5) “for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.” baptising her with the Holy Ghost.

Do you think she has ever regretted fully following Him? Or that anything but joy fills her heart? She is grateful for the path that brought her to this amazing place. Some of those steps were difficult at the time, but she doesn't regret them. If you want a blessing, give yourself completely to the Divine Master, just like she did. Don't hold back from any surrender, He asks of you .

The perfect way is hard to flesh. It is not hard to love. If you were sick and in need of God, how swiftly would you move? Surely, you can trust Him! Some may call for things of little worth to you. They may seem unworthy of the Lord's attention. Remember, He sees not as man sees, what is small to you may be, in His eyes, the key to the deepest thing. To shape you to His will, He must have you soft. This flexibility is more quickly reached by yielding in small things than in greater ones. Your one great desire is to follow Him fully; canst thou not say then a continual “Yes, Lord!” to all His sweet commands, small or great, and trust Him to lead you by the shortest road to your fullest Blessedness?

My dear friend, this, and nothing less than this, is what thy consecration meant, whether you knew it or not. It meant inevitable obedience. It meant that the will of your God was henceforth to be your will under all circumstances and at all times. It meant that, from then on, you gave up your freedom. You surrendered completely to your Lord's control. It meant an hour of following Him, wherever He led you. No dreams of turning back. Now, I ask you to keep your word. Let everything else go. Live, in daily life, the Divine life within you. You are united to your Lord by a wondrous tie. So, walk as He walked. Show the world His power to save by letting Him save you completely. You need not fear to consent to this, for He is your Saviour, and His power is to do it all. He is not asking you, in your weakness, to do it. He only asks you to yield to Him. Then, He will use His power to make you want to do it and to do it. Your job is to yield yourself. His is to work. He will never give you a command without giving you the power to obey it.

Do not worry about tomorrow. Trust your loving Lord. He promised to lead His sheep on a safe and easy path. Take each onward step as He makes it plain to you. Bring all your life in each of its details to Him to regulate and guide. Follow gladly and quickly the sweet suggestions of His Spirit in your soul. And, day by day, you will find Him. He will bring you more into conformity with His will in all things. He will, as you can bear it, shape you. Then, you will be a vessel of His honor, sanctified and ready for every good work. You will have the joy of being a letter of Christ, known and read by all.

Your light will shine so brightly that, seeing your good works, men will glorify your Father in Heaven, not you.

We are predestined to be “conformed to the image” of God’s Son. This means, of course, not a likeness of bodily presence, but a likeness of character and nature. It means a similarity of thought, of feeling, of desire, of loves, of hates. It means we should think and act, as Christ would, under our circumstances.

A little girl was once questioned what it meant to be a Christian. She replied, “It means to be just what Christ would be, if He was a little girl and lived in my house.” Th e secret of Christ's life was His selfless love for others. If we are like Him, this will be our secret too. He saved others, but Himself He could not save. He "pleased not Himself." So, we "not to please ourselves." Instead, we should please our neighbor, if it is for his good.

A thoughtful Hindu, who recently visited England and America to study Christianity, said, "What Christians need is a bit more of Christ's Christianity, and a bit less of man's." Man's Christianity teaches sacrifice to save oursel ves. Christ's Christianity teaches sacrifice to save others. Man’s Christianity produces the fruitless selfishness of too much of our religion. Christ's Christianity produces a blessed unselfishness. It comes from lives poured out for others, as was His. In short, our book teaches one thing: we are to be Christ like Christians. And all our experiences amount to nothing if they do not produce this result. "Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the w ill of my Father who is in heaven.” (Mathew 7:21)

Then, He will use His power to make you want to do it and to do it. Your job is to yield yourself. His is to work. He will never give you a command without giving you the power to obey it. Do not worry about tomorrow. Trust your loving Lord. He promised to lead His sheep on a safe and easy path. Take each onward step as He makes it plain to you. Bring all your life in each of its details to Him to regulate and guide. Follow gladly and quickly the sweet suggestions of His Spirit in your soul. And, day by day, you will find Him. He will bring you more into conformity with His will in all things. He will, as you can bear it, shape you. Then, you will be a vessel of His honor, sanctified and ready for every good work. You will have the joy of being a letter of Christ, known and read by all. Your light will shine so brightly that, seeing your good works, men will glorify your Father in Heaven, not you. We are predestined to be “conformed to the image” of God’s Son. This means, of course, not a likeness of bodily presence, but a likeness of character and nature. It means a similarity of thought, of feeling, of desire, of loves, of hates. It means we should think and act, as Christ would, under our circumstances. A little girl was once questioned what it meant to be a Christian. She replied, “It means to be just what Christ would be, if He was a little girl and lived in my house.” Th e secret of Christ's life was His selfless love for others. If we are like Him, this will be our secret too. He saved others, but Himself He could not save. He "pleased not Himself." So, we "not to please ourselves." Instead, we should please our neighbor, if it is for his good. A thoughtful Hindu, who recently visited England and America to study Christianity, said, "What Christians need is a bit more of Christ's Christianity, and a bit less of man's." Christ's Christianity produces a blessed unselfishness. It comes from lives poured out for others, as was His. In short, our book teaches one thing: we are to be Christ like Christians. And all our experiences amount to nothing if they do not produce this result. "Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the w ill of my Father who is in heaven.” (Mathew 7:21)

fields.title: The Joy Of Obedience
fields.body_html:
The Joy of Obedience emphasizes that true happiness comes from fully surrendering to God’s will. The author compares this surrender to a loving relationsh ip, where obedience to God brings intimacy and joy. While others may follow a more relaxed path, those who obey God experience a unique privilege and blessing. The message encourages believers to embrace complete obedience, which leads to spiritual fulfillment and divine rewards .

Ionce read: "Perfect obedience would bring perfect happiness if we had perfect confidence in the power we obeyed." It struck me. It revealed a possible, yet undreamed-of, way to be happy. Later, despite my lawlessness, that saying haunted me. It promised a rest and a way to grow. It soothed and satisfied my yearnings.

I must say, I have discovered this rest, not as a vision, but as a reality. I have seen in the Lord Jesus, our Master. We can yield to Him and take His yoke upon us to find perfect rest. You, dear, hesitant soul, don't know the joy you are missing. The Master has revealed Himself to you. He calls for your complete surrender. You shrink and hesitate. A measure of surrender you are willing to make, and think indeed it is fit and proper you should. But you seem to think that an utter abandonment, without any reserves, is too much to be asked for. You are afraid of it. It involves too much, you think, and is too great a task. To be obedient in a measurable way is your desire; the idea of being completely obedient appalls you.

You see other souls, too. They walk with easy consciences in a wider path than the one marked out for you. You ask yourself, why is this? It seems strange, and perhaps hard, that you must do what they need not. And, you must leave undone what they have the liberty to do. Ah! Dear Christian, this very difference between you is your privilege, though you do not yet know it. Your Lord says, "Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him.”(John14:21) You have His commandments; those you envy, have them not. You know the mind of your Lord about many things, in which, as yet, they are walking in darkness. Is not this a privilege? Is it regrettable that your soul is so close to your Master? He can tell you things that those farther away do not know. Do you not realize what a tender degree of intimacy this implies?

Many life relations require only a modest devotion from both parties. We may have great friendships.

Yet, we spend much of our lives in separate, differing pursuits. When together, we may enjoy each other's company. We may find many shared interests. But, we are not distressed by separation. Other, closer friendships do not interfere. We lack enough love to have the right or desire to share our most private affairs. A certain degree of reserve and distance is the suitable thing, we feel. But there are other relations in life where all this is changed. The friendship becomes love. The two hearts give themselves to one another, to be no longer two but one.

A union of souls takes place, which makes all that belongs to one the property of the other. Separate interests and separate paths in life are no longer possible. Things that were lawful before are now unlawful. It's due to the closeness of the tie that binds. The reserve and distance suitable for mere friendship become fatal in love. Love gives all, and must have all in return. One's wishes bind the other.

Each heart desires to know the other's secret wishes. It wants to fly on the wind to fulfill them.

Do people like this feel frustrated by the burden that love places on them? Do they envy the cool, calm friendships they see? Do they regret the closeness to their beloved because of the obligations it creates?

Do they not glory in these very obligations? And, with a tender, exulting joy, pity the poor, far-off ones who dare not come so near? Isn't every new revelation of each other's minds a delight? And, is any path hard that their love compels them to travel? Ah! Dear souls, if you've known this, even for a few hours; if you've ever loved someone enough to find joy in sacrificing for them; if you've ever longed to abandon your will to another as a sweet privilege, then, by all the love of your heavenly Master, I urge you to do the same for God!

He loves you with more than the love of friendship. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so does He rejoice over you. Only a full surrender will satisfy Him. He has given you all, and He asks for all in return. The slightest reserve will grieve Him to the heart. He spared not Himself, and how can you spare yourself? For your sake, He gave all He had. For His, you must do the same. Oh, be generous in your self-surrender! Meet His measureless devotion for you, with a measureless devotion to Him. Be glad and eager to throw yourself headlong into His dear arms, and to hand over the reins of government to Him. Whatever there is of you, let Him have it all. Give up forever everything separate from Him. I resign my freedom of choice. I rejoice in our union. It makes my devotion not just possible, but necessary.

Have you never longed to love someone far away? You were not close enough for a more intimate approach. Have you not felt a burning desire to surrender yourself to them? Yet, you had no one to whom you could give that love. Have not your hands been full of very precious, alabaster boxes of ointment? You have never been near enough to any heart to pour it out. If you hear your Lord's sweet voice, He is calling you to a place of closeness to Himself. It requires a separation from all else. It will make your devotion not just possible, but necessary. Will you shrink or hesitate?

Will you find it hard that He reveals more of His mind to you than to others? He will not let you be happy in anything that separates you from Himself. Do you want to go where He cannot go with you, or to have pursuits which He cannot share?

No! No, a thousand times, no! You will spring out to meet His dear will with an eager joy. Even His slightest wish will become a binding law to you, which it would fairly break your heart to disobey. You will rejoice in the narrowness of the path He sets for you. You will pity, with infinite sorrow, the poor, far-off ones who have missed this joy. Love's obligations will be its sweetest privileges. Your right to give your all to your Lord will feel like a lift into a realm of unspeakable glory. Perfect happiness will come from perfect obedience. You will then know a bit of what Jesus meant when He said, “ I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.”( Psalms 40:8 ) And do you think the joy in this will be all on your side? Has the Lord no joy in those who have thus surrendered themselves to Him, and who love to obey Him? Ah, my friends, we are unfit to speak of this. But the Scriptures reveal glimpses of the delight, satisfaction, and joy our Lord has in us. They ravish the soul with their wondrous hints of blessedness. That we should need Him is easy to comprehend; that He should need us seems incomprehensible. It is natural to desire Him. But that He should desire us is hard to believe. And yet, over and over, He says it, and what can we do but believe Him?

He has made our hearts able to feel this great love. He has offered Himself as its object. It is infinitely precious to Him. He says, “Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me.

And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him"(John 4:21). He knocks at every heart, seeking to be its supreme love. “Will you have me?” He says to the believer, “ To be your beloved, will you follow me into suffering and loneliness? Will you endure hardship for my sake? Ask for no reward but my smile and praise.

Will you throw yourself with an utter abandonment into my will? Will you give up to me the absolute control of yourself and all that you are? Will you be content with pleasing me and me only? May I have my way within you in all things? Will you come into so close a union with me as to make a separation from the world necessary? Will you accept me as your only Lord, and leave all others, to cleave only unto me?” In a thousand ways , He makes this offer of oneness with Himself to every believer. But all do not say “Yes,” to Him. Other loves and other interests seem to them too precious to be cast aside.

They do not miss Heaven because of this. But they miss an unspeakable joy.

You, however, are not one of these. From the very first your soul has cried out eagerly and gladly to all His offers, “Yes, Lord; yes!” You are more than ready to pour out upon Him all your richest treasures of love and devotedness. Your enthusiasm for self-surrender may disturb some moderate Christians.

Your love makes necessary a separation from the world, which a lower love cannot even conceive of.

Sacrifices and services are possible and sweet to you. They could not come from a less devoted heart.

The life upon which you have entered gives you the right to a lavish outpouring of your all upon your beloved One. Services, of which more distant souls know nothing, become now your sweetest privilege.

Your Lord claims from you, because of your union with Him, far more than He claims of them.

What to them is lawful, love has made unlawful for you. To you He can make known His secrets, and to you He looks for an instant response to every requirement of His love. Oh, it is wonderful! The glorious, unspeakable privilege upon which you have entered! It will matter little if men hate you. They may shun you, reproach you, and cast out your name as evil for His sake! "Rejoice in that day and leap for joy. Your reward is great in Heaven. If you share in His suffering, you shall share in His glory." In you He is seeing of the travail of His soul, and is satisfied. Your love and devotedness are His precious reward for all He has done for you.

It is unspeakably sweet to Him. Do not be afraid then to let yourself go in a heart-whole devotedness to your Lord that can brook no reserves. Others may not approve, but He will, and that is enough. Do not measure your obedience or your service. Let your heart and your hand be as free to serve Him, as His heart and His hand were to serve you. Let Him have all there is of you, body, soul, and spirit, time, talents, voice, everything. Lay your whole life open before Him that He may control it. Say to Him each day, “Lord, how shall I regulate this day so as to please you? Where shal l I go? What shall I do? Whom shall I visit? What shall I say?” Give your intellect up into His control and say, “Lord, tell me how to think so as to please you?” Give Him your reading, your pursuits, your friendships. Then say, "Lord, give me the insi ght to judge these things with your wisdom."” Do not let there be a day nor an hour in which you are not intelligently doing His will, and following Him wholly.

Serving Him will give your life a halo. It will gild even the dullest life with a heavenly glow.

Have you ever grieved that the romance of youth is so soon lost in the hard realities of the world? Bring God into your life and its details. A greater joy will thrill your soul than youth's brightest days could know. Nothing will seem hard or stern again. The meanest life will be glorified by this. As I watched a poor woman at her wash-tub, I thought of the disheartening aspects of her life. I wondered why such lives must exist. Then, with a thrill of joy, I recalled the possible glorification of it. I told myself, even this life, lived in and with Christ, following Him wherever He leads, would be glorious.

Every hour of it would be filled with enthusiasm.

I am comforted to know that God's greatest blessings lie with the poorest and most humble lives. "For," says our Lord Himself, "whosoever," whether rich or poor, old or young, bond or free.

Whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and my mother.

Pause a moment over these simple yet amazing words. His brother, sister, and mother! What would we not have given to have been one of these! Oh, let me beg you, beloved Christian. Come, taste and see how good the Lord is. He has wonderful things in store for those who "keep His commandments, and do what is pleasing in His sight." "If you listen closely to the Lord your God and obey all His commandments today, He will elevate you above all the nations on earth. If you listen to the Lord your God, all these blessings will come upon you."

“ Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your herds and the young of your flock. Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl. Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out. The LORD will cause your enemies who rise against you to be defeated before you. They shall come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways. (Deuteronomy 28:3-7) "T he LORD will command the blessing on you in your barns and in all that you undertake. And he will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you. The LORD will establish you as a people holy to himself, as he has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.” (Deuteronomy 28:8 -9) “ And all the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they shall be afraid of you. And the LORD will make you abound in prosperity, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, within the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you. The LORD will open to you his good treasury, the heavens, to give the rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. And the LORD will make you the head and not the tail, and you shall only go up and not down, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you today, being careful to do them,”(Deuteronomy 28:10 -13) For the Israelites, it was outward and temporary. For us, it is inward and spiritual. And, it is far more glorious. May our surrendered wills leap out to embrace it in all its fullness!

fields.title: Oneness With Christ
fields.body_html:
God’s purpose is to unite believers with Himself through Christ. True oneness with He is shown in living His will, character, and actions, not just in emotions. It requires surrender, obedience, and a Christ-like life, fully aligning with His purpose.

God's dealings with a believer's soul aim for oneness with Himself. This fulfills the Lord's Prayer: “that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. The glory that you have given me I have given to them, that they may be one even as we are one, I in them and you in me, that they may become perfectly one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them even as you loved me"(John 17:21-23) God's glorious purpose for His people, before the world's foundation, was a soul-union. It was the mystery hid from ages and generations. It was accomplished in the incarnation of Christ. It has been made known b y the Scriptures. And it is realized as an actual experience by many of God’s dear children. But not by all. It is true of all. God has not hidden it. But, many have dim eyes and unbelieving hearts. They fail to grasp it. The Lord is stirring up believers everywhere. He wants them to abandon themselves to Him. It is to bring them to a personal realization of this. He wants to work in them all the good pleasure of His will.

All the previous steps in the Christian life lead up to this. The Lord has made us for it. Until we know it, and choose to embrace it, His soul's travail for us is unsatisfied. Our hearts have not found their final rest.

Then they followed Him, worked for Him, believed in Him, and yet, how unlike Him! They sought to be above each other. They ran from the cross. They misunderstood His mission and words. They forsook Him in danger. Yet, He sent them to preach. He recognized them as His disciples, with power to work for Him. They knew Christ only “after the flesh,” is outside of them, their Lord and Master, but not yet their Life.

Then came Pentecost. These disciples then knew Him as revealed within. They were one with Him, their very indwelling Life. Henceforth, He was to them Christ within. He worked in them to will and to do of His good pleasure.

He, by the law of the Spirit of His life, delivered them from the bondage to the law of sin and death, under which they had been held. No longer was it between themselves and Him, a war of wills and a clashing of interests. One will alone animated them, and that was His will. One interest alone was dear to them, and that was His. They were made ONE with Him.

Surely, all can recognize this picture. But the final stage may not be fully reached. You may have left much to follow Christ, dear reader. You may have believed in, worked for, and loved Him. Yet, you may not be like Him. Allegiance, you know, and confidence you know, but not yet union. There are two wills, two interests, two lives. You have not yet lost your own life that you may live only in His.

Once it was I and not Christ. Then it was I and Christ. Perhaps now it is even Christ and me. But has it come to be Christ only, and not I at all? They hope to find, in these, their union with God. But nowhere is the mistake of trusting to feelings greater than here.

Oneness with Christ must, by nature, mean a Christ-like life and character. It is not what we feel, but what we are that settles the question. No matter how strong our feelings, there can be no oneness without a likeness of character with Christ. We must share a unity of aim, purpose, and thought. Our actions must be similar, too.

This is common sense, and it is Scriptural too. We say two people are one. We mean their purposes, actions, thoughts, and desires are alike. A friend may express great love and unity. But if their aims, actions, and views are the opposite of ours, we can't feel any real oneness. This is true despite our affection for each other. To be truly one with another, we must share everything. Our likes and dislikes, joys and sorrows, hopes and fears, must all be the same. As someone says, we must look through one another’s eyes, and think with one another’s bra ins. This is, as I said above, only plain common sense.

And oneness with Christ can be judged by no other rule. It is out of the question to be one with Him in any other way than in the way of nature, character, and life. Unless we are Christ-like in our thoughts and our ways, we are not one with Him, no matter how we feel. I have seen Christians with few Christ- like traits. They were so emotional and ecstatic in their love for Christ that they believed they were justified in claiming a close oneness with Him. I scarcely know a sadder sight. Surely our Lord meant to reach such cases when He said, “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.” (Mathew 7:21.)

He w as not making here any arbitrary statement of God’s will, but a simple announcement of the nature of things. Of course it must be so. It is like saying, “No man can enter the ranks of astronomers who is not an astronomer.” Emotions will not make a man an a stronomer, but life and action. He must be one, not merely feel that he is one.

There is no escape from this inexorable nature of things, and especially here. We must be one with Christ in character, life, and action. If not, we cannot be one with Him in any other way. There is no other way. We must be "partakers of His nature" to share His life. His life and His nature are one.

But emotional souls do not always see this.

They feel so near to Christ and so united to Him that they think it must be real. They overlook the need for a Christ-like character and walk. So, they build their hopes on their delightful emotions and exalted feelings. They believe they must be one with Him to have such rich, holy experiences.

It is a fact that other causes can produce these emotions. They are not solely due to a divine influence.

The emotions depend largely on temperament and physical conditions. It is most dangerous, therefore, to make them a test of our spiritual union with Christ. It may result in just such a grievous self-deception as our Lord warns against in (Luke 6:46-49): “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I tell you? Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you what he is like: he is like a man building a house, who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. And when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house and could not shake it, because it had been well built. But the one who hears and does not do them is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream broke against it, it immediately fell, and the ruin of that house was great.”

Our soul delights in calling Him, "Lord, Lord." But, are we doing what He said? He tells us this is the important point, after all.

If, led by our feelings, we claim to abide in Him in meetings, among friends, or in our hearts before the Lord, let us consider these words of the Holy Ghost: "He that says he abides in Him, ought himself so to walk, even as He walked." Unless we are walking as He did, we cannot be abiding in Him, no matter how much we may feel we are.

If you are one with Christ, you will be sweet to those who are cross with you. You will bear everything and make no complaints. When reviled, you will not revile again. You will consent to be trampled on, as Christ was, and feel only love in return. You will seek others' honor rather than your own. You will take the lowest place and serve all, as Christ did. You will truly love your enemies and do well to those who spitefully use you. In short, you will live a Christ-like life. You will show and feel, a Christ-like spirit and walk among men as He did. This, dear friends, is what it is to be one with Christ. If this is not your life, you are not one with Him. Your feelings, no matter how ecstatic, do not matter.

To be one with Christ is too wonderful and solemn a thing. It is too mighty an experience to be reached by mere feelings. He was holy, and those who are one with Him will be holy also. There is no escape from this simple and obvious Fact.

When our Lord tried to show His oneness with God, He said, “And he who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”(Joshua 8:29) “So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of his own accord, but only what he sees the Father doing. For whatever the Father does, that the Son does likewise. For the Father loves the Son and shows him all that he himself is doing. And greater works than these will he show him, so that you may marvel. For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he will. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, that all may honor the Son, just as they honor the Fat her. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him” (John 5:19-23) The test of oneness, then, was the doing of the same works, and it is the test of oneness now. If our Lord could say that, so must His disciples. He said to believe in Him only if He did the works of His Father. He asked for no belief based on His claims.

A healthy tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a diseas ed tree bear good fruit” (Mathew 7:17 -18 ). It is not that they will not, but they cannot. A soul united with Christ will, for sure, bear a Christ-like life. A grapevine bears grapes, not thistles. I don't object to emotions, though. I don't want to base our faith on them. Let them come or let them go, just as God pleases, and make no account of them either way. But, we must have the vital marks of oneness with Christ. We must share a likeness in character, life, and walk. If we do, all will be well. For “ Whoever says 'I know him' but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him, but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we may know that we are in him: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked.” (1John 2:4 -6) It may be, my dear reader, that the grief of your life has been the fact that you have so few good feelings.

You try your hardest to get up the feelings that you hear others talking about, but they will not come.

You pray for them fervently and are often tempted to upbraid God because He does not grant them to you. You are filled with unbearable anguish. You think your lack of emotion means your soul is not united with Christ. You judge altogether by your feelings, and think there is no other way to judge.

The Bible teaches, if nothing else, this: A Christ-like life must accompany any true experience of His spirit. It could not be otherwise in the very nature of things. But I fear some Christians have separated the two things so much that they now value their experiences over their walk. They care more about their feelings than their character. A certain colored congregation in one of the Southern States was a plague to the whole neighborhood. They openly disregarded even the ordinary rules of morality. But, it always brings a coldness over the meetings when I preach about these things." You are helpless as to your emotions, but you can have character if you will. You can be so filled with Christ as to be Christ-like. If you are Christ-like, then you are one with Him in the only vital, essential way. Your feelings may say it's impossible, but they are wrong.

If you read such passages as ( 1 Corinthians 3:16), “ Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you ?” Then, look at the chapter's opening. It shows to whom these wonderful words are spoken. They are for babies in Christ, who were yet carnal and walked according to man. This soulunion, this glorious mystery of an indwelling God, is the possession of even the weakest and most failing believer in Christ.

So that it is not a new thing you are to ask for, but only to realize that which you already have. It is absolutely true for every believer in the Lord Jesus. His "body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, who is in him, who is of God.”

He longs to be known to them, to share their daily lives and interests. But, He won't force Himself upon them. Only a voluntary companionship could satisfy His love. The days pass over that favored household. They remain unaware of their great privilege. They come and go about all their daily affairs with no thought of their wonderful Guest.

Their plans are laid without reference to Him. His wisdom to guide, and His strength to protect, are all lost to them. Lonely days and weeks are spent in sadness, which might have been full of the sweetness of His presence. Every moment might have been spent in the sunshine of His sweet presence. Every step might have been taken under His advice. But because you did not know it, and have never looked for Him, your life has been lonely and full of failure. But now that I announce to you, how will you receive it? Are you glad to have Him? Will you throw wide open every door to welcome Him in? Will you joyfully and thankfully give up the governance of your life into His hands?

Will you consult Him about everything, and let Him decide each of your steps, and mark out every path? Will you invite Him to your innermost chambers, and make Him the sharer in your most hidden life? Will you say, YES to all His longing for union with you, and with a glad and eager abandonment, will you, then, hand yourself and all that concerns you over into His hands? If you will, then shall your soul begin to know something of the joy of union with Christ.
